Left-wing councils warn they'll defy new rules on single-sex spaces as they claim guidance is 'harmful to the rights of trans people'
- See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source
A group of Left-wing councils have warned they will defy new rules on single-sex spaces as they claimed the guidance is 'harmful to the rights of trans people'.
Local leaders from six London boroughs - Lambeth, Waltham Forest, Southwark, Hackney, Haringey and Lewisham - said they could resist guidance prepared by the Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC).
A new code of practice on the Equality Act 2010, including the use of toilets and changing rooms as single-sex spaces, came into force on Wednesday.
It set out single-sex toilets, changing rooms, hospital wards and refuges must be used based on a person's birth sex, not the gender with which they identify.
The guidance has been issued after a landmark Supreme Court ruling on biological sex in April last year, which saw judges state the words 'woman' and 'sex' in the Equality Act 2010 refer to a biological woman and biological sex.
In an open letter to Labour's Bridget Phillipson, the women and equalities minister, the six leaders and other senior councillors said it was 'simply unacceptable' that the new guidance 'is harmful to the rights of trans people and will make their exclusion from public life more likely, not less'.
They added: 'This will feel like an attack to the countless trans people in our communities who are simply trying to live their lives in safety and wish to be treated with respect.'
The Green and Liberal Democrat-led councils warned they would not 'put our staff in the impossible position of policing entry to public spaces' and said they were now 'reviewing all of our internal practices to ensure that no trans person is excluded on the basis of our actions'.
A transgender flag flies in front of Parliament during the Trans Pride march in Westminster last year
It comes after Lambeth councillors last month backed a call for the council to refuse to implement the EHRC's amended code of practice.
The councils demanded that Ms Phillipson confirm the new guidance 'cannot be used to exclude trans people from services'; introduce legislation to 'protect the rights of trans and non-binary people'; and 'create an equalities framework that protects trans people's safety, dignity and humanity'.
They wrote in their letter: 'We say this to you in no uncertain terms: Trans women are women, trans men are men, and non-binary identities are fundamentally valid.
'As councils who are proud to be boroughs of sanctuary, with significant LGBTQ+ communities, we are committed to being safe, welcoming and inclusive places for all residents, regardless of their background or identity.
'We have an unshakeable commitment to ensuring that Trans+ residents can access services safely, with dignity and free from discrimination or harassment.
They added: 'The Government's own Equalities Impact Assessment acknowledges that there is a real risk Trans+ people could face exclusion, discrimination, or difficulties accessing services if organisations misinterpret the ruling, based on appearance alone.
'Overly broad enforcement can, and will, lead to trans and non-trans people alike being challenged and excluded from services and facilities.
'Meanwhile, the code introduces a dangerous lack of clarity for us as service providers, leaving our staff at risk of inadvertent discrimination where no third spaces are available to Trans+ people. We won't put our staff in the impossible position of policing entry to public spaces.
'We stand in solidarity with trans people, an already marginalised community subject to increasing discrimination.
'This Government claims it is standing up for equality. That can never be the case while the rights of trans people are treated as an afterthought.'

items.title: Liverpool weigh up hijacking £60m Arsenal transfer to appease desperate Andoni Iraola
items.summary: Andoni Iraola is desperate for a signing in central defence, where Liverpool are "very thin", and the club could beat Arsenal to Aston Villa and England star Ezri Konsa
items.body_text:
Liverpool weigh up hijacking £60m Arsenal transfer to appease desperate Andoni Iraola
Andoni Iraola is desperate for a signing in central defence, where Liverpool are "very thin", and the club could beat Arsenal to Aston Villa and England star Ezri Konsa
Liverpool could rival Arsenal for the signing of Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa as Andoni Iraola desperately seeks a solution to his injury crisis. Pre-season has shown just how short Liverpool are in central defence, providing some urgency to their search for a new centre-back.
An injury to Joe Gomez in a friendly against Sunderland has highlighted the lack of depth in the position, with £55million signing Jeremy Jacquet yet to feature in pre-season as he's eased back from a shoulder injury and Giovanni Leoni still recovering from his ACL injury.
With Virgil van Dijk given time off after the World Cup, Iraola has been forced to turn to youth, starting Ifeanyi Ndukwe, 18, and Luke Chambers, 22, in the 4-2 defeat by Leeds on Sunday, while Mor Talla Ndiaye, 18, has also featured in pre-season.
The departure of Ibrahima Konate means Liverpool need an experienced player to partner Van Dijk and the Guardian reports that Konsa has emerged as a target. The England international is also on Arsenal's radar after William Saliba suffered a back injury at the World Cup, but Villa's £60m valuation is thought to be beyond the Gunners' means.
FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page
Konsa has two years left on his contract at Villa, where he has played since 2019, making 286 appearances in all competitions. The 28-year-old has a wealth of Premier League experience and could fit the bill for Iraola, who has voiced frustrations at the lack of depth in the squad he inherited this summer.
Jacquet, who signed in January from Rennes, and Victor Munoz (£35m from Osasuna) are the only two major deals done so far and the issue is shown by the fact Iraola's assistant, Tommy Elphick, had to fill in at centre-back in a recent training drill.
Iraola admitted recently: "With the centre-back, with the right-back situation, in terms of defensive depth, we are, I think, very thin right now so I think it's a solution that we are trying to find, yes."
Gomez will miss the Premier League opener against Newcastle on August 23, leaving Van Dijk as the only fit senior centre-back in the squad. The Dutchman did not join his team-mates on the United States leg of their pre-season, leaving Iraola will less time to work with him before the campaign kicks off.
"When the market is open, you have to be always open to new options to improve the squad," Iraola said last month. "There are obvious situations where we need to sign players."
Liverpool are undergoing a summer of transition, with Iraola arriving to replace Arne Slot after a disappointing campaign, which saw Konate, Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson leave. To complicate matters further, Fenway Sports Group chief Michael Edwards has also left, piling more pressure and responsibility onto sporting director Richard Hughes to get deals done.

items.title: Does the dad in My Life with the Walter Boys die?
items.summary: My Life with the Walter Boys ended on not one but two cliffhangers in the epic season two finale.
items.body_text:
Does the dad in My Life with the Walter Boys die?
My Life with the Walter Boys ended on not one but two cliffhangers in the epic season two finale.
My Life with the Walter Boys season three has finally revealed George Walter’s fate.
Almost a year ago, Netflix fans were left desperate to find out what happens next after My Life with the Walter Boys' second series concluded with an almighty finale.
Jackie Howard (played by Nikki Rodriguez) had reunited with her first Silver Falls romance Alex Walter (Ashby Gentry) but feelings clearly still lingered for his older brother Cole (Noah LaLonde).
This burning desire eventually resurfaced in the final scene where Jackie and Cole confessed their love for one another but much to their horror, Alex heard everything.
But before he could react, Will Walter (Johnny Link) suddenly arrived with ambulances following closely behind, with him simply stating: “It’s dad.”
Does the dad in My Life with the Walter Boys die?
Netflix
In the build-up to the season two cliffhanger, George Walter (played by Marc Blucas) had been working in the ranch’s top field. He had been dealing with a lot of stress thanks to conflicts over land development and it was Will who found him collapsed before alerting the rest of the family.
The opening moments of My Life with the Walter Boys season three shows George being rushed into hospital with a doctor telling the family that it was a suspected stroke.
A montage shows the family trying to cope with the aftermath and George still lying in a hospital bed unconscious and Katherine Walter (Sarah Rafferty) by his side.
Thankfully, George Walter doesn’t die in season three as he’s next seen sitting up in hospital as Cole helps his father have a drink of water.
Sharing what fans can expect from season three going forward, showrunner Melanie Halsall said: “Jackie is desperately trying to bring the family together.
“There’s a part of her that feels like she’s responsible for what happened to George because she feels that she just messed everything up in those last few moments of season two.”
Halsall goes on to tease that series three kicks off with an “emotional” first episode and that “a lot of this season, more than other seasons, is about growing up, maturing, and stepping up.”
Alex Walter star Ashby Gentry also commented to Tudum: “Everyone’s reality has shattered a little bit, and they’re picking up the pieces of that and trying to put it back together again.”

items.body_text:
After Michigan, Wisconsin Democrats now face a party divide in key gubernatorial and congressional primary elections
The slew of Democratic primaries underscores a growing divide within the party
- Bookmark
- CommentsGo to comments
After progressive Dr. Abdul El-Sayed swept to a stunning victory in Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary earlier this week, eyes are turning to a flurry of Democratic primaries in Wisconsin. 
Similar to Michigan’s tight-necked race, the Democratic primary for the gubernatorial race later this year has underscored a growing divide between the party’s establishment and more left-wing.
Four candidates remain in the race, which takes place on August 11 - the same day as a slew of Congressional races, three of which have become electoral flashpoints.
Unlike in Michigan, there is no Senate primary on the ballot in Wisconsin when voters go to the polls.
The Democratic Gubernatorial Race
Democratic socialist Francesca Hong has attracted much of the press attention in the race so far, having been criticized over previous calls to defund the police and to cancel Thanksgiving. The professional chef later walked back those comments, saying Turkey Day is actually her “favorite” holiday, according to The Hill.
While Hong stated during the Democratic gubernatorial debate that as governor, she could not defund law enforcement.
The state representative is running on a slew of left-wing policies, including free school meals, universal child care, developing new BadgerCare programs and guaranteeing paid leave for all workers. 
Hong is facing off against three other candidates, including Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, who has been endorsed by outgoing Governor Tony Evers. 
On his campaign website, Crowley says that his lived experience has informed how he would govern. 
“David never knew if he would come home from school to find his family's belongings on the curb due to another eviction, food in the kitchen, or the heat and lights still on,” the website reads, adding that both of his parents battled addiction and mental health struggles.
Policies focusing on the cost of living and making the state more affordable have formed the bedrock of his campaign.
Also in the running is state Senator Kelda Roys, who has pledged to make the state entirely powered by clean energy in 2050 and to allow Wisconsinites to buy into the same health insurance that state employees have. Roys’ allies have painted her as being a meticulous politician.
“She wants to break down every tiny piece,” Carousel Bayrd, a former Dane County supervisor, told Wisconsin Public Radio. “I think that that’s what sets her apart. The level of intentional attention to detail.”
The fourth candidate is Joel Brennan, a former secretary of the Wisconsin Department of Administration.
On his campaign website, Brennan touts his economic credentials and says that he built a budget surplus worth nearly $4 billion while in Governor Evers’ cabinet. 
“I grew up the tenth of eleven kids in Wisconsin, a family long on potential, sometimes short on resources,” he said. “My parents made sure we understood that if you worked hard and showed up, this state would give you a shot.”
Brennan added, “That's the Wisconsin I believe in, and it's the Wisconsin I'm fighting to protect.”
Whoever wins on August 11 will go head-to-head with Republican Representative Tom Tiffany, whom Trump has given his “Complete and Total Endorsement” on social media.
Congressional District 1
Democrats in this district are hoping to defeat U.S. Representative Bryan Steil.
Mitchell Berman, an ER nurse, is running against rivals Lorenzo Stantos and Miguel Aranda.
Berman has often referenced his healthcare background in his campaign, while Stantos has focused on raising the minimum wage. Aranda has focused on supporting unions and immigration reform.

items.title: Newsom trolls Trump for ‘very low energy’ visit to California
items.summary: Gov. Gavin Newsom brands President Donald Trump’s brief trip to his state ‘a total snoozer’
items.body_text:
Newsom trolls Trump for ‘very low energy’ visit to California
Gov. Gavin Newsom brands President Donald Trump’s brief trip to his state ‘a total snoozer’
- Bookmark
- CommentsGo to comments
California Gov. Gavin Newsom has delivered a damning verdict on President Donald Trump’s latest trip to the Golden State, calling it “very low energy.”
“Trump’s visit to California was a total snoozer,” the Democrat posted on his press office account on X. “Very low energy. No speech. He could barely take a question on the tarmac.”
He was responding to a clip of Trump turning away from reporters on the runway at Los Angeles International Airport and trudging back towards the steps of Air Force One, batting away a question about beleaguered Ohio Republican Rep. Max Miller.
In a further comment on his personal account, he added: “Trump talks tough from inside his Truth Social bubble, but suddenly has nothing to say when he’s actually in California.
“While the president uses L.A. to raise campaign cash, survivors of last year’s firestorms are waiting for him to finally deliver federal relief to recover.”
The president flew west on Tuesday to headline a Republican National Committee fundraiser at his Trump National Golf Club in Rancho Palos Verdes, also taking part in a roundtable event and giving an interview to Fox News reporter Trace Gallagher before moving on to Las Vegas, Nevada.
Trump did not meet with Newsom nor deliver a speech on his first visit to the state since January 2025, when he sparred with the governor after arriving to survey the destruction wrought by the Palisades Fire.
The president and the governor again clashed the following June after Trump sent federal immigration troops into downtown Los Angeles to round-up people accused of being in the country illegally, sparking protests and prompting him to send in the Marines and National Guard against Newsom’s wishes.
Ahead of the president’s return trip this week, the governor attacked him on social media over the minimum wage, saying that California was raising it to $17.40 an hour from next year, which he pointed out was more than double the federal level.
“Donald Trump and the GOP are still defending a $7.25 minimum wage while workers scrape by,” he added. “Pitiful.”
Retaliating, White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales briefed that Trump would use his appearance in front of the RNC to deride Newsom’s policies, accusing the governor of raising taxes, allowing fraud in taxpayer-funded programs and protecting dangerous undocumented immigrants.
Following the president’s departure, the governor responded to a post from Wales saying as much, with the comment: “We’re old enough to remember when the White House fed The New York Post a quote saying Trump would ‘target’ the governor during his trip yesterday to Los Angeles – instead silence.”
He cited three conservative sources who had repeated Wales’s line and said they “got played like fools” and had been “used and discarded” by the White House.
The governor has made waves over the last year by regularly spoofing Trump online, parodying his idiosyncratic posting style and firing out memes and videos ridiculing his public performances, moving many to tip him as a possible Democratic presidential nominee come 2028.
In another post reacting to the president’s passing visit, he wrote: “California’s win rate against the Trump administration in court is 83 percent.”
He has since gone after the president for claiming during a speech at the Red Rock Casino Resort and Spa in Las Vegas Wednesday that his tariffs program had “made us rich.”
“Us = billionaires and big corporations,” Newsom qualified.

items.body_text:
Where extreme heat is having the biggest impact on Americans’ lives, according to a new AP-NORC poll
A new AP-NORC poll finds that Americans are increasingly noticing the impact of extreme heat on their lives, and they say much of that shift is happening in the West and Midwest
- Bookmark
Elisa Bracamonte has lived in Arizona her whole life, so she's used to adjusting her schedule and outdoor activities around high temperatures, especially during the summer months.
But the 74-year-old retired nurse from Tucson said she feels the heat has been impacting more of her day-to-day: summer plans with family members across the region, meetups with friends, road trips and her daily morning walk routine.
"I’ve noticed at least a 10 degree difference in the weather," Bracamonte said. “Every summer, it seems to be getting hotter and hotter.”
Like Bracamonte, Americans are increasingly feeling a personal impact from extreme heat, according to a new poll from The Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research.
According to the survey, U.S. adults are more likely to say extreme heat has had either a “major impact” or “minor impact” on their travel or vacation plans, electricity bills, their sleep, their family’s outdoor activities and more parts of their day-to-day life than in July 2024.
Much of that shift was among people who live in the West or Midwest.
Democrats are also more likely than Republicans to say that extreme heat has had a “major” impact on each item asked about.
Warming has endangered the globe especially in recent years; scientists calculated that Earth’s average temperature in 2025 hovered among one of the three hottest on record, along with 2024 and 2023. The U.S. has sweltered under dangerous heat domes over the past few years, and unusually high temperatures even early in the year.
The recent scorching weather has played a role in thousands of heat-related deaths — killing more people every year than all other weather-related events. It impacts wildfire risk, strains public infrastructure, devastates agriculture and wreaks havoc on gatherings such as sporting events.
Now, the poll shows how extreme heat is reshaping Americans' daily lives.
“I have to get up at 5 in the morning to walk before 6, because by 7 it’s already in the 80s ... I lose a couple hours of sleep because I’m having to wake up earlier,” added Bracamonte, who said she identifies as a very liberal Democrat. “You can’t stay outside without being sick unless you’re guzzling water the whole time — it’s just so, so hot.”
Electricity bills going up
About 8 in 10 Americans say their electricity bills have seen a “major” or “minor” impact from extreme heat over the last year, compared with 69% in July 2024, according to the survey.
Just under half of Americans living in the Midwest, 44%, say extreme heat has had a “major” impact on their electricity bills, up from 29% two years ago.
Rising household electricity prices have turned into an increasingly prominent political issue over the past few years. Extreme weather is just one factor that affects electricity bills, but it means that people are using more energy for air conditioning — or in the colder months, heat.
“I feel like my utility costs probably doubled in the last three or four years,” said Daemien Williams, a 50-year-old bridge inspector living in Cahokia Heights, Illinois, who identifies as a Democrat. “I do look at my bills pretty in detail and see that the kilowatts and the usage is actually up, not just the price that they’re charging for it."
Travel and vacation plans impacted, along with family outdoor activities
Extreme heat is affecting Americans' lives in other ways, the survey found.
Around 4 in 10 Americans say extreme heat has had either a major impact or a minor impact on their travel or vacation plans, up from about one-quarter in 2024.

items.title: How Ukraine’s relentless strikes on Russia could actually boost Putin
items.summary: Drone attacks on Russian territory in recent months have raised fears of a backlash against Kyiv
items.body_text:
On a quiet Monday near the Russian resort town of Gelendzhik, people were sunbathing and paddling when a drone erupted from the skies, hurtling downwards to explode on the sand. Videos circulating online showed holidaymakers watching with faces to the sky as the drone came down, and wading out of the sea as plumes of smoke rose.
At least seven people, including three children, were reported to have been killed and 40 injured in the attack, which Russia has blamed on Ukraine. It is not clear what the drone was targeting or whether it had veered off course due to a malfunction, direction error or electronic warfare, which can interfere with the signal between drone and controller. Ukraine has not commented on the incident but has repeatedly said it does not target civilians.
The beach blast was the latest in a wave of explosions inside Russia designed to hit the Kremlin where it hurts. In recent weeks, Ukraine has targeted logistics hubs and energy sites, with a series of strikes on warehouses belonging to Wildberries, Russia’s version of Amazon, and now reportedly targeting its second-largest e-commerce company, Ozon.
Shorts
Eight people were killed in Russia during separate drone attacks over the weekend. Russia has also blamed Ukraine for a bomb attack on a restaurant in Moscow that killed five people, with speculation the target was a senior Russian military commander reportedly celebrating his birthday, but this has not been confirmed.
Analysts have warned that Vladimir Putin could use the attacks as anti-Ukraine propaganda to shore up support for his invasion.
Tim Willasey-Wilsey, a former British diplomat, warned that Ukrainian attacks risked increasing criticism of Kyiv and strengthening Russian support for the war. “Ukraine’s targeting policy has been carefully calibrated to focus on petrochemical industries and dual-use supply chains. But, as we know from history – not least the London Blitz – the bombing of civilians tends to antagonise people and reinforce, rather than weaken, morale,” he told The i Paper.
While Russia has been “targeting civilians since day one” – with daily ballistic missile attacks on Kyiv “killing civilians by the dozen”, Willasey-Wilsey said that Ukraine “will be held to a higher standard” because it is a Western ally and democratic country.
“The occasional error by Ukraine will be understood by the international community, like the drone on the beach, but it must not become normalised,” said Willasey-Wilsey, who is now a senior associate fellow at defence think-tank Rusi.
In the first six months of the year, Russia reported that 250 of its civilians had been killed and 1,596 injured, a 121 per cent increase compared with the same period in 2025, according to figures shared with the UN.
The figures pale in comparison to the number of Ukrainian civilians killed by Russia since it launched a full-scale invasion four years ago. At least 293 civilians were killed and 1,990 injured in Ukraine in June alone, UN figures show – the highest monthly death toll since April 2022, shortly after the war began.
Civilian casualties in Ukraine have risen steadily from month to month and from year to year, amid intensifying use of powerful weapons, the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine has warned. In the first six months of 2026, 1,396 civilians died and 7,978 were injured – a 37 per cent rise from the same period in 2025, and a 114 per cent increase compared with the year before.
Dr Marina Miron, a researcher at King’s College London’s War Studies team, said that Ukraine’s hopes of galvanising Russian opinion against the war through strikes on infrastructure and factories could well backfire.
“It is difficult to measure the overall impact on society because there will be those who might turn against the war, but not necessarily against the Kremlin,” Miron said.

items.title: My predicted England XI to face Pakistan as first Test squad of new era is named
items.summary: There are some eye-catching picks and a significant nod to county cricket in the first squad since Brendon McCullum and Ben Stokes vacated their roles as coach and captain
items.body_text:
If England’s squad for the first two Tests against Pakistan is anything to go by then the new era under Joe Root’s captaincy will place a greater emphasis on county cricket and aim to fill the void left by Ben Stokes’ retirement by packing out the bowling.
The main headline from the 16-man party selected for the opening two matches at Headingley, starting on 19 August, and Lord’s later this month is the absence of Jacob Bethell.
The 22-year-old has failed to recover from a knee injury sustained during the one day-series against India last month and will be replaced at No 3 in England’s batting line-up by Jordan Cox.
It’s a bold call to pick a player with just one Test appearance at such a pivotal position. But England clearly rate the Essex batter and he has a huge opportunity against Pakistan given Bethell is out for the entire series.
Equally bold is going back to Dan Lawrence at No 6, the Surrey batter’s back two years after his last Test appearance at home to Sri Lanka at The Oval.
Lawrence is the second-leading runscorer in this year’s County Championship, with 788 at an average of 65. His average of 26 across his first 14 Tests was not helped by being asked to bat in the top order for many of those games, including opening in all three Tests against Sri Lanka in his last series.
Lawrence’s part-time spin is a sign that despite Shoaib Bashir being in the squad, England are likely to go with an all-seam attack unless they are presented with a pitch that looks like it is going to turn square.
Balancing the side effectively without the all-round talents of Stokes was always going to be a tricky task. This way, England hope they have not weakened the batting and have given themselves enough depth in the bowling department to cover for the loss of Stokes, who announced his shock international retirement during the final Test against New Zealand at Trent Bridge in June.
The significant nod to county cricket is underlined by the recalls of Ollie Pope – ostensibly as cover for wicketkeeper Jamie Smith and Cox at No 3 – for the first time since last winter’s Ashes and Essex seamer Sam Cook.
The squad was picked by Root, director of cricket Rob Key and national selector Marcus North. New Test coach Stephen Fleming, who will not start his job until the winter tour of South Africa, also had an input from afar.
It appears a significant break from the Bazball era, when players were often picked on hunches by former Test coach Brendon McCullum and captain Stokes.
Two notable absentees in spinning all-rounders Rehan Ahmed and Will Jacks, both of whom would have hoped to have batted at No 6 instead of Lawrence, illustrate this shift.
Brydon Carse, back from a hand injury that forced him to miss the first half of the summer, returns and will be competing for one of the four seam-bowling spots.
However, it seems likely that a fully-fit Ollie Robinson, man-of-the-match in England’s win against New Zealand at Lord’s in June, will take his place in the attack alongside Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson and Josh Tongue.
	
My prediced England XI for Headingley
- Ben Duckett
- Emilio Gay
- Jordan Cox
- Joe Root (captain)
- Harry Brook
- Dan Lawrence
- Jamie Smith (wicketkeeper)
- Gus Atkinson
- Ollie Robinson
- Jofra Archer
- Josh Tongue
North said of the squad: “We have selected a squad for the first two Tests that balances rising talent with the experience needed against a quality Pakistan team.
“Dan Lawrence returns following an exceptional season so far with Surrey and we believe he has the right level of experience, maturity and skill to complement our middle order.
“Jordan Cox is well regarded as one of the most exciting talents in English cricket and will have the opportunity to bat at three in place of Jacob Bethell, who sadly misses this series through injury.”

items.title: Stop feeling sorry for ‘boy mums’ – girls aren’t any easier to parent
items.summary: Science shows it's a myth that girls are inherently quiet and compliant while boys are active and rowdy, and it harms us all
items.body_text:
“My sons are absolute chaos at home,” a friend recently lamented, wishing they would sometimes sit quietly and draw “like girls do”. Yet, when her son came to my house for a playdate, he sat and drew happily for with my children, a boy (7) and girl (9), who both sometimes sit and draw for hours on end.
Another time when my son crashed his bike into a stationary car, another mother remarked: “That’s just boys for you.” In reality, it was just bad luck and the accident had nothing to do with his gender.
All too often, at the school gate and on social media I hear parents talk about how rough and loud boys are compared to girls, and how socially complex girl friendships are. I tend to offer a counter view -and explain that both my children can be noisy and both enjoy quiet activities.
But the myths that girls are naturally meeker and more emotional while boys are louder and harder work when young, persist. These stereotypes have damaging consequences for girls and boys.
Shorts
The real reason your daughter likes princesses, even though you raised her gender neutral
As a science journalist and author, I’ve spent years reporting about child development. Experts have consistently told me that children are like little detectives who work out early on which “gender tribe” they belong to. As toddlers, they then gravitate to play, toys and behaviour that fit with their group.
While boys do tend to take part in more boisterous physical play and girls tend to express bigger emotions, this does not mean one sex is inherently harder to parent than the other.
“It’s a misconception,” says neuroscientist and gender scholar Lise Eliot, at Rosalind Franklin University of Medicine and Science. She stresses that every child is different and behavioural overlaps between boys and girls are larger than any differences.
“There is no such thing as a male brain and a female brain, except for size [proportional to body size]” Eliot tells me. “We’re just so invested in gender.”
Part of the reason the myth persists is that we start treating children differently before they can even speak. For instance, fathers of daughters have been found to use more language relating to emotions, while fathers of sons use more achievement-related language.
The earlier children enter nursery, the earlier the gendered behaviours starts. Parents around me will often lament and say they tried to parent in a “gender neutral” way, but still find their daughters prefer princesses. This leads many to conclude that it must just be how they are wired. An assumption that ignores the fact that children tend to be more heavily influenced by their peers than by what toys we give them at home.
Gender stereotypes shape behaviour from the beginning
Social conditioning also shapes play and behaviour far earlier than most parents realise. When a friend’s twin boys came over for a play date, the first item they gravitated to was a toy buggy, much to their mother’s surprise. It was simply not something she had at home.
Studies show that boys do show interest in playing with dolls until they become aware it could be perceived as a “girl toy”, after which they have been found to play with dolls secretly or not at all.
Similarly, girls do not emerge from the womb naturally preferring pink or dolls, but are more often presented with toys that encourage nurturing play. Children therefore figure out early on which category they belong to and adjust their behaviour accordingly, says Eliot.
Boys are not naturally more active
If girls are expected to sit quietly and repeatedly encouraged to do so at home and in the classroom, this will predispose them to being more compliant overall, whereas noisy behaviour among boys is expected and therefore excused.

items.title: Iran, Oman move to finalize new Hormuz shipping corridor
items.summary: TEHRAN — Facing dwindling strategic resources after months of military confrontation with Iran, the United States has increasingly pinned its hopes on negotiations between Tehran and Muscat to secure the future of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's most strategically important maritime corridors.
items.body_text:
Iran, Oman move to finalize new Hormuz shipping corridor
An informed source says agreement with Oman does not mean the opening of the Strait of Hormuz
TEHRAN — Facing dwindling strategic resources after months of military confrontation with Iran, the United States has increasingly pinned its hopes on negotiations between Tehran and Muscat to secure the future of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's most strategically important maritime corridors.
While Washington initially sought to address the issue through broader diplomatic arrangements following the 40-day conflict, the collapse of the Islamabad Memorandum has left the Iran-Oman channel as the principal avenue for any future settlement governing the Strait.
The shift reflects a new geopolitical reality that has emerged following the conflict. Beyond the military costs of the war, the United States has reportedly seen significant depletion of both its missile stockpiles and strategic petroleum reserves, while the prolonged disruption of shipping through the Strait has intensified pressure from global energy markets and America's regional partners to restore maritime commerce.
Against this backdrop, Washington has increasingly focused on supporting indirect diplomacy, allowing two neighboring states with direct geographical sovereignty over the Strait—Iran and Oman—to negotiate a new framework for navigation.
Economic shockwaves reinforce Strait's strategic importance
The urgency surrounding the negotiations has been reinforced by newly released international trade data.
According to analysis published by the United Nations and the International Trade Centre (ITC), the disruption of shipping through the Strait has produced one of the most severe shocks to global commodity markets in recent years.
Exports of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from economies dependent on the route have fallen by 95 percent, while urea exports have dropped 83 percent.
Japan, which previously sourced more than 90 percent of its crude oil imports through the region, has experienced a 64 percent decline in imports despite efforts to diversify suppliers.
The figures suggest that alternative supply chains have failed to fully offset losses originating from the Persian Gulf, underscoring the global consequences of prolonged instability in the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran-Oman talks reach critical stage
Iranian and Omani negotiators are now believed to be in the final stages of discussions over a memorandum of understanding that would establish new shipping arrangements for the waterway.
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei has said the negotiations focus on ensuring safe maritime navigation while preserving the sovereign rights and security interests of both countries.
According to informed Iranian sources, the proposed agreement goes beyond simply defining new navigation lanes.
Tehran has reportedly insisted that once the new maritime corridor is formally incorporated into the memorandum, subsequent negotiations should also establish mechanisms governing maritime management, security coordination and navigational services.
Iranian officials view these issues as inseparable from the country's sovereign rights over one side of the strategically vital waterway.
Washington watches from the sidelines
Although the negotiations are formally being conducted between Iran and Oman, Western media reports indicate that the United States remains closely engaged in developments.
Reuters reported that the draft framework under discussion could allow Iran to oversee vessels entering the Persian Gulf through designated shipping lanes while negotiations continue over outbound traffic.
The Financial Times similarly reported that the White House has closely monitored progress through Omani mediation, with Washington increasingly viewing the Iran-Oman channel as its best opportunity to reduce tensions after the failure of previous diplomatic initiatives.

items.title: “The Lucky Ride” at Iranian bookstores
items.summary: TEHRAN- A Persian translation of Japanese writer Yasushi Kitagawa’s book “The Lucky Ride: A Novel Full of Opportunity” has recently been published by Milkan Publications in Tehran.
items.body_text:
“The Lucky Ride” at Iranian bookstores
TEHRAN- A Persian translation of Japanese writer Yasushi Kitagawa’s book “The Lucky Ride: A Novel Full of Opportunity” has recently been published by Milkan Publications in Tehran.
The book has been translated into Persian by Zahra Chaflaki.
“The Lucky Ride” is about a man who believes himself to be the unluckiest person in Japan—a man whose life has been a relentless sequence of disappointments, failures, and missed opportunities. For years, he has viewed his existence through the lens of misfortune, convinced that he was born under a darkened star and that the universe is fundamentally rigged against him. However, his life takes a surreal and transformative turn when a mysterious driver appears, offering him a ride that is far more than a mere trip from one location to another. This encounter serves as the catalyst for the ride of a lifetime, pushing the protagonist to step out of his cycle of despair and seize a new, unexpected path.
Blending the whimsical "what-if" exploration of “The Midnight Library” with the revelatory, mindset-shifting power of “The Secret,” Yasushi Kitagawa crafts a heartwarming parable about the architecture of happiness. As the journey unfolds, the story evolves into a deep exploration of self-growth and emotional healing. The protagonist is forced to confront the ghosts of his past, seek reconciliation with loved ones, and rediscover a sense of purpose that he had long since abandoned.
The core philosophy of “The Lucky Ride” is that luck is not a random gift granted to a chosen few, nor is it a genetic trait. Instead, the narrative proposes that luck is a result of the conscious choices we make and the positive energy we project into the world. Through the guidance of the mysterious driver, the protagonist learns that the bad luck he clung to was often a reflection of his own resignation. He discovers that by shifting his perspective and embracing a spirit of gratitude and openness, he can actually build his own fortune over time.
This Japanese bestseller is a compassionate reminder that true fulfillment does not come from the absence of struggle, but from the courage to keep moving forward with a good heart. Kitagawa illustrates that the treasures of a meaningful life are built incrementally, one choice at a time, and that this positive legacy can be passed down through generations.
SAB/

items.title: UN experts say Iran steps up repression of ethnic minorities
items.summary: Iran has intensified its repression of ethnic minorities, particularly Kurdish and Baluch communities, through arbitrary arrests, enforced disappearances and executions, a group of UN human rights experts said on Thursday.
items.body_text:
"The psychological impact is what these attacks are intended to do,"said Annie Fixler, director of the Center on Cyber and Technology Innovation at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD).
"Iranian hackers in particular conduct what's called perception hacking," she said. 
"They conduct a small-scale operation, they get into a network, they take a couple pictures of what they got, and then they claim to have caused a massive disruption because they're trying to cause a psychological impact even when they can't cause an actual true cyber impact."
Federal authorities last week warned that "malicious cyber actors" had targeted water and wastewater systems across at least seven states, with Minnesota reporting the largest number of incidents after around 30 water systems were disrupted. Officials urged utilities to disconnect vulnerable internet-connected equipment and switch to manual operations where necessary.
The FBI has opened an investigation but has not publicly attributed responsibility. However, multiple US media outlets, citing government officials familiar with the investigation, reported that Iran is the leading suspect.
President Donald Trump dismissed suggestions that Tehran was responsible, instead blaming Minnesota Governor Tim Walz, while Walz argued the attacks illustrated "what modern warfare looks like."
Why Iran?
Although no official attribution has been made, cybersecurity specialists say several characteristics of the campaign closely resemble previous Iranian operations.
"The particular systems they attacked are programmable logic controllers," Fixler said, referring to industrial control devices widely used in water facilities.
"The US government warned repeatedly earlier this year that Iranian actors were targeting those particular systems."
Earlier this year, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned that Iranian-affiliated hackers were actively targeting internet-connected operational technology, including programmable logic controllers used in water infrastructure.
The agency later updated its advisory with additional guidance on securing vulnerable equipment.
Unlike financially motivated ransomware attacks, the latest incidents included no ransom demands.
"The first thing I look for is whether there's a ransom request," Fixler said. "We haven't seen that."
That absence points away from criminal hackers and toward a geopolitical operation, she said.
Amin Sabeti, a cybersecurity researcher specializing in Iranian cyber operations, said the campaign also reflects the typical strengths and limits of Iran's cyber capabilities.
"I don't think it was sophisticated, but it was a clever one," Sabeti said.
Rather than deploying cutting-edge exploits, he said the attackers appeared to exploit weak cybersecurity practices such as unchanged default passwords and poorly secured internet-connected equipment.
Compared with Russia and China, "they are a small boy in the town," Sabeti said, arguing Iranian operators excel at social engineering and exploiting simple vulnerabilities more than conducting highly sophisticated cyber campaigns.
A familiar playbook
The suspected campaign would fit a pattern established over recent years.
In late 2023, the IRGC-linked hacking group CyberAv3ngers targeted water facilities in Pennsylvania by compromising Israeli-made Unitronics programmable logic controllers, forcing operators to switch to manual controls.
Iran has also targeted Israeli water infrastructure. In 2020, Iranian hackers attempted to manipulate chlorine levels in Israeli water systems, according to Israeli and Western officials, prompting a reported Israeli cyber retaliation against Iran's Shahid Rajaee Port.

items.title: Executions in Isfahan renew calls to end German city partnership
items.summary: The public execution of two protesters in Isfahan has renewed calls for the German city of Freiburg to end its 25-year twinning with the Iranian city, with activists arguing the partnership lends legitimacy to a state punishing dissent with death penalty.
items.body_text:
The demands follow the executions of Amirhossein Safari and Abolfazl Sepahi in Isfahan's Alikhani Square in late July. Witnesses reported clashes between security forces and people who gathered to protest the hangings.
Freiburg, a university city in southwestern Germany, is the only municipality in the country to maintain a formal partnership with an Iranian city. Iranian activists have long argued that the arrangement, established in 2000, legitimizes the Islamic Republic despite its human rights record.
Mayor Martin Horn has rejected those arguments. Speaking to Frankfurter Rundschau in June, he said, "We as a city do not conduct foreign policy," adding that shutting the door on Isfahan would undermine engagement with ordinary Iranians. 
"People are reaching out to the West, and we slam the door shut? That is exactly the opposite of what we should be doing."
‘Nothing against Isfahan’
Germany-based dissident Mina Ahadi, who led a successful international campaign against Iran's practice of public stoning, said the latest executions had fundamentally changed the debate.
"I have been protesting for a long time against this twin-city partnership between Freiburg and Isfahan because it is, in reality, a relationship with the state structures of the Islamic Republic," she told Iran International.
"I therefore support the numerous protests and demands to end this partnership—especially in light of the current tragedy in Isfahan: the public execution of two young people and the threat of the death penalty facing further individuals in this city."
Ahadi said ending the partnership would not be directed against the people of Isfahan but would instead demonstrate solidarity with Iranians confronting state repression.
"It would be a sign of support for the people in Iran, who themselves are victims of the policies of the Islamic Republic," she said.
‘Unjustifiable’
Behrouz Asadi, spokesperson for Woman Life Freedom Germany, likewise argued that the partnership had ceased to function as a neutral cultural exchange.
"The twin-city partnership between Freiburg and Isfahan has clearly shown in recent years that it is not an apolitical cultural exchange," he said. "As long as the Islamic Republic controls the exchange, such a partnership primarily serves its propaganda and grants legitimacy to its networks—not to the people of Isfahan."
He said recent executions, alongside the imprisonment of activists and members of the Baha'i community, made it increasingly difficult to justify maintaining the relationship.
"The people of Isfahan have taken to the streets for freedom, democracy and human dignity," Asadi said. "
Many have suffered prison, torture or even death for it. It is not justifiable toward them to maintain a partnership that creates the impression that normal cultural exchange with this regime is possible."
Defense of human rights
The debate has also drawn attention to Baden-Württemberg's antisemitism commissioner, Michael Blume, whom some critics accuse of failing to challenge the Freiburg-Isfahan partnership. Blume did not respond to repeated requests for comment from Iran International.
The partnership has faced criticism before. In 2010, the German city of Weimar ended its relationship with Shiraz after Iranian officials visiting Germany refused to visit the Buchenwald concentration camp memorial.
For campaigners, however, the executions in Isfahan have raised the stakes beyond a long-running dispute over municipal diplomacy.
They argue the question is no longer whether cultural engagement remains desirable, but whether maintaining official ties with an Iranian municipality can be reconciled with a rapidly deteriorating human rights situation.
“Verbal distancing is no longer enough,” said Asadi. “Anyone who takes human rights seriously must draw consequences. That is why I demand the termination of the twin-city partnership with Isfahan.”

items.body_text:
کارشناسان سازمان ملل خواستار توقف سرکوب اقلیتهای اتنیکی در ایران شدند
گروهی از کارشناسان سازمان ملل با اشاره به افزایش بازداشتهای خودسرانه، ناپدیدسازی قهری، شکنجه و اعدام اعضای اقلیتهای اتنیکی در ایران، از جمهوری اسلامی خواستند به سرکوب کردها و بلوچها و اقدامات فرامرزی علیه مخالفان پایان دهد.
کارشناسان سازمان ملل پنجشنبه ۱۵ مرداد در بیانیهای مشترک اعلام کردند اقلیتهای اتنیکی در ایران باید بتوانند بدون تبعیض و در امنیت و با کرامت زندگی کنند.
مای ساتو، گزارشگر ویژه سازمان ملل درباره وضعیت حقوق بشر در ایران، موریس تیدبالبینز، گزارشگر ویژه اعدامهای فراقضایی، شتابزده یا خودسرانه، نازیلا قانع، گزارشگر ویژه آزادی دین یا عقیده و نیکولا لورا، گزارشگر ویژه مسائل اقلیتها، از جمله امضاکنندگان این بیانیه هستند.
بر اساس این بیانیه، از آغاز اعتراضات دیماه ۱۴۰۴ تاکنون، مقامهای جمهوری اسلامی هزاران نفر را بازداشت کردهاند. بنا بر گزارشهای دریافتی، بسیاری از بازداشتشدگان برای گرفتن اعتراف تحت شکنجه یا دیگر اشکال بدرفتاری قرار گرفتهاند.
کارشناسان گفتند در موارد متعدد، افرادی که در ارتباط با اعتراضات از آزادی محروم شدهاند، قربانی ناپدیدسازی قهری بودهاند؛ به این معنا که مقامها بازداشت یا محل نگهداری آنان را تایید نکردهاند و خانوادههایشان از سرنوشت آنها بیخبر ماندهاند.
در بیانیه آمده است گزارشها از افزایش چشمگیر بازداشتهای خودسرانه و صدور احکامی حکایت دارند که ظاهرا انگیزه سیاسی دارند. اعضای اقلیتهای اتنیکی نیز اغلب با استناد به اتهامهای امنیتی دارای تعریف گسترده بازداشت و محاکمه میشوند.
کنشگران بر این باورند که جمهوری اسلامی بهویژه پس از تنشهای نظامی اخیر قصد دارد با ایجاد فضای رعب و وحشت، مانع از فوران دوباره خشم عمومی علیه بحرانهای فزاینده معیشتی و سیاسی شود.
اعدام دستکم ۲۴ شهروند بلوچ و ۲۲ شهروند کرد در سال ۲۰۲۶
بر اساس بیانیه کارشناسان سازمان ملل، تنها در سال ۲۰۲۶، دستکم ۲۴ شهروند بلوچ و ۲۲ شهروند کرد اعدام شدهاند.
آنها هشدار دادند شمار بیشتری از اعضای این دو اقلیت با خطر قریبالوقوع اجرای حکم اعدام روبهرو هستند.
کارشناسان سازمان ملل به قانون مصوب سال ۱۴۰۴ درباره گسترش تعریف جاسوسی اشاره کردند و گفتند این قانون و اتهامهایی مانند «محاربه»، «افساد فیالارض» و «بغی»، به ابزاری برای سرکوب مخالفتها، بهویژه در مناطق کردنشین، تبدیل شدهاند.
آنها همچنین برای جلوگیری از اعدام پنج زندانی، شامل چهار شهروند کرد و یک شهروند بلوچ، درخواست اقدامی فوری کردند.
یوسف احمدی، رئوف شیخ معروفی، محمد فرجی و محسن اسلامخواه، چهار شهروند کرد، و فرهاد برانزهی، شهروند بلوچ، پس از رسیدگیهایی قضایی که بنا بر گزارشها با شکنجه و اعترافات اجباری همراه بوده است، در معرض خطر قریبالوقوع اعدام قرار دارند.
کارشناسان پرونده این افراد را بخشی از الگوی گستردهتر و سازمانیافته سرکوب اقلیتهای کرد و بلوچ دانستند. آنان همچنین به احکام اعدام صادرشده برای پخشان عزیزی و وریشه مرادی اشاره کردند.
در این بیانیه آمده است اعضای اقلیتهایی که هویت اتنیکی و مذهبی آنان با یکدیگر همپوشانی دارد، از جمله کردهای سنی و پیروان آیین یارسان، در دورههای ناآرامی سیاسی و اجتماعی بیشتر هدف قرار میگیرند.
به گفته کارشناسان، روایتهای رسمی این افراد را تهدیدی برای امنیت ملی معرفی میکنند و زمینه بازداشت، تعقیب قضایی و صدور احکام سنگین علیه آنان را فراهم میسازند.
کارشناسان سازمان ملل همچنین از افزایش بازداشتهای خودسرانه و ناپدیدسازی قهری اعضای دیگر اقلیتهای اتنیکی، از جمله آذربایجانیها، ابراز نگرانی کردند.
افراد زیر سن قانونی نیز بنا بر گزارشها در میان بازداشتشدگان بودهاند.
ائتلاف «ایمپکت ایران» پیشتر در بیانیهای از جامعه جهانی خواست مساله حقوق بشر را همزمان با مذاکرات امنیتی و هستهای با جمهوری اسلامی، در دستور کار قرار دهند.
سرکوب فرامرزی مخالفان جمهوری اسلامی
بر اساس بیانیه کارشناسان سازمان ملل، سرکوب اقلیتهای کرد و بلوچ به داخل مرزهای ایران محدود نمانده است.
مقامهای جمهوری اسلامی متهم شدهاند که از تهدید، نظارت و تعقیب افراد ساکن خارج از کشور بهعنوان ابزاری برای «سرکوب فرامرزی» استفاده میکنند.
کارشناسان گفتند مقامهای حکومت ایران اموال صدها ایرانی خارج از کشور را توقیف کردهاند.
آنان همچنین به انتشار فهرستی شامل نام ۳۷ رهبر و فعال کرد ساکن خارج از ایران اشاره کردند که با صدور احکام غیابی و درخواستهای استرداد همراه بوده است.
در بیانیه آمده است قوانین مبارزه با تروریسم در داخل ایران و در سطح فرامرزی بهشکلی نادرست علیه اقلیتها مورد استفاده قرار میگیرند.

items.title: نشریه پیام ما: صنعت گردشگری ایران عملا به تعطیلی کشیده شده است
items.summary: نشریه «پیام ما» در گزارشی وضعیت صنعت گردشگری ایران را «تعطیلی کامل» توصیف کرد و نوشت درآمد بسیاری از فعالان این حوزه از خرداد سال گذشته تاکنون صفر یا منفی بوده است؛ بحرانی که حتی با دستیابی به توافق سیاسی نیز به‌سرعت پایان نخواهد یافت.
items.body_text:
نشریه پیام ما: صنعت گردشگری ایران عملا به تعطیلی کشیده شده است
نشریه «پیام ما» در گزارشی وضعیت صنعت گردشگری ایران را «تعطیلی کامل» توصیف کرد و نوشت درآمد بسیاری از فعالان این حوزه از خرداد سال گذشته تاکنون صفر یا منفی بوده است؛ بحرانی که حتی با دستیابی به توافق سیاسی نیز بهسرعت پایان نخواهد یافت.
بر اساس این گزارش، بسیاری از کسبوکارهای گردشگری در ماههای گذشته با وجود نداشتن درآمد، برای حفظ کارکنان خود هزینه حقوق و بیمه پرداختهاند و در نتیجه زیان بیشتری متحمل شدهاند.
ادامه بحران، برخی شرکتها را به تعدیل نیروهای متخصص واداشته است. شماری از فعالان نیز صنعت گردشگری یا ایران را ترک کردهاند و به برخی دیگر توصیه شده است برای تامین هزینههای زندگی، دستکم بهطور موقت به مشاغلی خارج از این حوزه روی بیاورند.
پیام ما تاکید کرد مشکلات صنعت گردشگری ایران فقط نتیجه جنگ، تحریم یا وضعیت سیاسی نیست.
ضعف زیرساختهای حملونقل، بیثباتی اقتصادی، شیوههای سنتی مدیریت، ارتباط محدود علمی و حرفهای با جهان و نبود برنامهای مشخص برای بازگرداندن گردشگران، مجموعهای از موانع ساختاری ایجاد کردهاند.
به نوشته این نشریه، حتی در صورت دستیابی به توافق سیاسی یا برقراری صلح، برطرف کردن این موانع به زمان و برنامهریزی گسترده نیاز خواهد داشت.
حملونقل به مانع گردشگری تبدیل شده است
در مقاصد گردشگری موفق، زیرساخت حملونقل معمولا ابتدا برای پاسخگویی به نیاز ساکنان توسعه مییابد و گردشگران نیز از آن استفاده میکنند.
پس از افزایش ورود مسافر، سرمایهگذاریهای تازه برای گسترش مقصد و ایجاد مسیرهای متناسب با نیاز گردشگران انجام میشود.
در ایران، مشکلات حملونقل به یکی از موانع اصلی فعالیتهای گردشگری تبدیل شده است.
نشریه پیام ما با اشاره به همین موضوع نوشت دشواری رزرو بلیت قطار، محدودیت ظرفیت و نبود امکان رزرو گروهی، برنامهریزی برای تورهای ریلی را بسیار محدود یا در مواردی ناممکن کرده است.
لغو پروازها در شرایط جنگی برای حفظ امنیت مسافران اجتنابناپذیر است، اما به نوشته پیام ما، کنسلی و تاخیر ناشی از کمبود زیرساخت یا تصمیمهای ناگهانی، حتی سفرهای عادی داخلی را نیز مختل میکند.
بر اساس این گزارش، در چنین شرایطی، سخن گفتن از توسعه گردشگری معنای چندانی ندارد.
این گزارش همچنین به هدایت ناوگان اتوبوسرانی به سوی مرزها در «زمانهای خاصی از سال» اشاره کرد.
پیام ما افزود در نخستین سال اجرای این تصمیم، رزرو اتوبوسهای مورد نیاز تورهای ورودی بدون اطلاع قبلی لغو شد و برگزارکنندگان نتوانستند به تعهدات خود در برابر گردشگران خارجی عمل کنند.
تکرار چنین شرایطی سبب شد بسیاری از فعالان گردشگری در این بازههای زمانی از بازاریابی و فروش تور خودداری کنند؛ تصمیمی که بخشی از بازار فصلی ورود گردشگران خارجی به ایران را از بین برد.
۱۲ مرداد، در پی بسیج امکانات عمومی از سوی جمهوری اسلامی برای مراسم اربعین، شهروندان از اختلال در حملونقل، کمبود کالا و فشار بر خدمات عمومی خبر دادند.
این نخستین بار نیست که بسیج امکانات عمومی برای مراسم اربعین به اختلال در خدمات و انتقادهای گسترده منجر میشود.
در سالهای اخیر هزینههای سنگین جمهوری اسلامی برای برگزاری این مراسم، همزمان با نادیده گرفتن مشکلات داخلی، بارها با اعتراض شهروندان روبهرو شده است.
بیثباتی ارز قیمتگذاری تورها را ناممکن کرده است
به گزارش پیام ما، یکی دیگر از مشکلات اصلی صنعت گردشگری، نبود قطعیت مالی است.
افزایش ناگهانی نرخ ارز و تغییر لحظهای قیمت خدمات، امکان ارائه قیمت مشخص به تورگردانها و مسافران خارجی را از بین برده است.
برنامهریزی برای سفرهای بینالمللی معمولا از ماهها قبل آغاز میشود و گاهی شرکتها و گردشگران یک یا دو سال پیش از سفر برای رزرو تور اقدام میکنند.
در چنین بازاری، شرکتی که نتواند قیمت و خدمات خود را برای آینده تضمین کند، عملا امکان رقابت حرفهای ندارد.
برخی پژوهشها نشان میدهند جریان گردشگری پس از تثبیت شرایط سیاسی و امنیتی، در صورت وجود برنامهریزی و تلاش منسجم، معمولا طی شش ماه تا یک سال به مقصد بحرانزده بازمیگردد.
پیام ما اما شرایط ایران را متفاوت دانست و نوشت ایران پیش از بحرانهای اخیر نیز جایگاه برجستهای در بازار گردشگری خاورمیانه نداشت.
آسیب دیدن اعتبار بینالمللی کشور و نبود برنامهای مدون برای جلب دوباره گردشگران میتواند روند بهبود را طولانیتر کند.
بر اساس گزارش، حتی پس از دستیابی به توافق احتمالی و برقراری صلح، ممکن است دستکم دو سال زمان لازم باشد تا نخستین نشانههای بهبود در گردشگری ایران مشاهده شود.

items.summary: باشگاه رئال مادرید برای به‌خدمت‌گرفتن یان دیومانده، وینگر ۱۹ ساله اهل ساحل عاجِ لایپزیگ، با این تیم آلمانی به توافق رسید.
items.body_text:
توافق برای انتقال دیومانده؛ رکورد گرانترین خرید تاریخ کهکشانیها خواهد شکست؟
باشگاه رئال مادرید برای بهخدمتگرفتن یان دیومانده، وینگر ۱۹ ساله اهل ساحل عاجِ لایپزیگ، با این تیم آلمانی به توافق رسید.
بر اساس گزارش نشریه «اتلتیک»، ارزش این معامله شامل ۱۲۵ میلیون یورو مبلغ ثابت، بههمراه ۱۵ میلیون یورو پاداش متغیر است که در مجموع میتواند به ۱۴۰ میلیون یورو برسد.
با نهایی شدن این انتقال، دیومانده از رقم ۱۲۷ میلیون یورویی جود بلینگام در سال ۲۰۲۳ پیشی میگیرد و به گرانترین بازیکن تاریخ رئال مادرید تبدیل خواهد شد.
این پدیده اهل ساحل عاج که فصل گذشته با ثبت ۱۳ گل و ۱۰ پاس گل در ۳۶ بازی، درخشش چشمگیری داشت، تا سال ۲۰۳۰ با لایپزیگ قرارداد دارد.
در حالی که پیشتر صحبت از حضور او در پاریسنژرمن مطرح بود، دیومانده پس از انصراف باشگاه پاریسی، رئال مادرید را بهعنوان اولویت اصلی خود انتخاب کرد.
این بازیکن ۱۹ ساله در حال حاضر منتظر تأیید نهایی باشگاه آلمانی است تا برای انجام معاینات پزشکی و امضای قرارداد رسمی، عازم مادرید شود.
•
روزنامه دیلی تلگراف به نقل از منابع آگاه نوشت که دونالد ترامپ، رییس جمهور آمریکا برای جلوگیری از برکناری جیانی اینفانتینو از ریاست فیفا، پس از جنجال طرح فروش بخشی از سهام جام جهانی، «هر کاری از دستش بربیاید انجام خواهد داد.»
اینفانتینو پس از شکست طرح ۱۵ میلیارد پوندی (۲۰ میلیارد دلاری) خود برای خصوصیسازی داراییهای تجاری فوتبال، با فشار فزایندهای برای استعفا روبهرو شده است.
گزارشهایی که روز دوشنبه ۱۲ مرداد منتشر شد، حاکی از آن بود که اینفانتینو قرار است با اعضای کابینه ترامپ، از جمله مارکو روبیو، وزیر خارجه آمریکا، دیدار کند تا جایگاه خود را تقویت کند. فیفا و وزارت امور خارجه آمریکا این گزارشها را رد کردند.
با این حال، یکی از مقامهای ارشد دولت آمریکا که به هر دو نفر نزدیک است، به دیلی تلگراف گفت ترامپ پس از آنکه اینفانتینو به آمریکا برای برگزاری «بهترین جام جهانی تاریخ» کمک کرد، به او علاقهمند شده و مایل است او در سمت خود باقی بماند.
جام جهانی امسال زمانی با جنجال روبهرو شد که ترامپ اعلام کرد از اینفانتینو خواسته است محرومیت فولارین بالوگان برای دیدار مرحله یکهشتم نهایی آمریکا برابر بلژیک لغو شود.
این منبع گفت: «جیانی کمک بزرگی کرد تا بهترین جام جهانی تاریخ را برگزار کنیم. رییسجمهوری او را بسیار دوست دارد. مطمئنم هر کاری بتواند برای کمک به او انجام خواهد داد.»
او افزود: «فکر نمیکنم رییسجمهوری نظرش را درباره او تغییر دهد، چون فردی وفادار است. جیانی جام جهانی را برای آمریکا به بهترین شکل برگزار کرد و ما برای این موضوع ارزش قائلیم.»
پیش از این جنجال، گزارش شده بود ترامپ علاقه دارد اینفانتینو دبیرکل بعدی سازمان ملل متحد شود؛ سازمانی که ترامپ بارها گفته دیگر کارآمد نیست.
اینفانتینو که از سال ۲۰۱۶ ریاست فیفا را بر عهده دارد، در نخستین دیدار خود با ترامپ در اوت ۲۰۱۸ با همراه داشتن کارتهای قرمز و زرد، توجه او را جلب کرد و با شوخی گفت این کارتها «ممکن است هنگام برخورد با رسانهها به کارتان بیاید.»
از آن زمان، روابط این دو نزدیکتر شده است.
در مراسم قرعهکشی جام جهانی در ماه دسامبر، اینفانتینو «جایزه صلح فیفا» را به ترامپ اهدا کرد؛ اقدامی که پس از ناکامی او در دریافت جایزه صلح نوبل، که بارها علاقه خود به آن را ابراز کرده بود، انجام شد.
ترامپ همچنین یک جام طلایی با نام خود و یک مدال یادبود دریافت کرد.
نیویورکپست روز دوشنبه گزارش داد اینفانتینو پس از شکست طرح فروش بخشی از جام جهانی، تلاش کرده با ترامپ تماس بگیرد اما موفق نشده است.
ترامپ نیز روز جمعه در پاسخ به پرسشی درباره این طرح گفت از زمان مطرح شدن این موضوع، با اینفانتینو گفتوگو نکرده است.
پائولو زامپولی، فرستاده ویژه آمریکا در امور مشارکتهای جهانی، گفت: «کارنامه جیانی اینفانتینو حفظ انحصار فوتبال برای ثروتمندترین نهادهای این ورزش نیست، بلکه گسترش فوتبال به کشورهای بیشتر، جوامع بیشتر و کودکان بیشتر است.»
او افزود: «او به نگرانیها گوش داد و طرح را کنار گذاشت؛ همان کاری که یک رهبر باید انجام دهد. اکنون بحث اصلی این است که چگونه ثروت و فرصتهای فوتبال به همه ۲۱۱ کشور عضو برسد، نه اینکه فقط در اختیار گروهی محدود باقی بماند.»

items.title: UKMTO Says Explosions Reported In Strait Of Hormuz
items.summary: As the conflict in the Persian Gulf continues to impact and shape the region, journalists from RFE/RL's Central Newsroom and Iranian service, Radio Farda, deliver ongoing updates and analysis.
items.body_text:
2 Iranian Soccer Players Become Australian Citizens After Seeking Asylum
Fatemeh Pasandideh and Atefeh Ramezanizadeh, two former members of the Iranian women's national soccer team who sought refuge in Australia at the start of the US-Israeli war with Iran and during the Asian Cup, have been granted Australian citizenship.
After Iranian national team players were accused of "treason" for not singing the national anthem in their first game, which coincided with the first days of the war, several members of the team decided to stay in Australia.
As pressure on these players increased and following reports of their families in Iran being harassed, most of them returned to Iran, but Pasandideh and Ramezanizadeh remained in Australia.
Australian Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke offered the two players humanitarian visas in March, and they officially became Australian citizens on August 5 at a citizenship ceremony in Brisbane.
2 Explosions Reported Near Oil Tanker In Strait Of Hormuz
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Organization (UKMTO) announced on August 6 that an oil tanker had reported several explosions while passing through the Strait of Hormuz near the coast of Oman.
This comes as officials from Iran's Foreign Affairs Ministry say they are in talks with Oman for joint management of the strategic waterway.
"The Master of a tanker has reported hearing two explosions while transiting in the Strait of Hormuz," the UKMTO said on X.
The incident occurred 9 nautical miles southeast of the Omani coast late on August 5.
The organization added that based on the report received, the crew and the ship are safe and no environmental damage has been reported.
Iran, which has closed the Strait of Hormuz on several occasions since the start of the US-Israeli war against it, has previously opened fire on ships that Tehran says did not pass through designated "authorized routes."
Trump: 'I'd Rather Make a Deal' With Iran Than Resort to Military Action
US President Donald Trump said on August 5 that he would prefer to reach a diplomatic agreement with Iran rather than launch further military action, while reiterating that Tehran must not acquire nuclear weapons.
Speaking in Las Vegas, Trump said: "We're either going to make a deal or we're going to finish the job. And it won't be tough to finish the job. I'd rather make a deal, because I don't want to affect 91 million people."
Trump also claimed Iran had sought talks after the United States was on the verge of carrying out what he described as a much larger military strike, saying continued military pressure had brought Tehran back to the negotiating table.
The remarks came as the Trump administration said it would continue negotiations with Iran, with discussions including the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
US Senator John Curtis Points To Bipartisan Momentum As Russia-Iran Sanctions Bill Nears Final Vote
WASHINGTON -- A bipartisan coalition in the US Senate is working to keep momentum behind a sweeping sanctions package targeting Russia and Iran, with lawmakers from both parties arguing that the legislation would send a broader message about American resolve against authoritarian powers.
Republican Senator John Curtis of Utah, a member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, the unusually broad support for the measure reflects a growing recognition in Congress that Russia's war against Ukraine is not simply a regional conflict but a test of the international order.
The Senate advanced the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act in a key procedural vote last week, with Curtis serving in the presiding chair during the vote. Speaking with RFE/RL on August 5, he said the level of bipartisan backing was significant.
"It's not very often that you see things here in the Senate that are that overwhelmingly bipartisan," Curtis said. "And when you see that many of my colleagues on both sides come together, you should pay attention because that means we're serious and something's going to hap

items.title: Germany Probes 'Hybrid Attack' At Leipzig Airport After Explosive Drone Found Near Ukrainian Plane
items.summary: German authorities are investigating two "very serious security incidents" at the Leipzig/Halle airport that temporarily suspended and diverted flights, raising suspicions of Russian involvement after similar incidents in recent years.
items.body_text:
German authorities are investigating two "very serious security incidents" at the Leipzig/Halle airport that temporarily suspended and diverted flights, raising suspicions of Russian involvement following similar incidents in recent years.
The Leipzig Police Directorate said in a statement that late on August 4, "an unidentified flying object" was sighted near the airport, prompting the diversion of several aircraft, including a passenger plane, to other airports.
A drone carrying a "suspicious object" was also discovered in the vicinity of one of the two main runways.
The Dresden Public Prosecutor's Office and the Saxony State Criminal Police Office, which are leading the investigation, said the drone discovered on the runway was carrying "an unknown explosive device."
"With the support of the Federal Police and a bomb disposal robot, the object was examined. The Federal Police's IED unit removed the detonator," it said.
Operations on the airport's north runway resumed early on August 5, but the south runway, where the object on the ground was found, remains closed as police investigate, authorities said.
"The incidents at Leipzig Airport constitute a very serious security incident," Minister of State for the Interior Armin Schuster said in a separate statement.
Several German media outlets, including Bild, reported that the drone was discovered in the immediate vicinity of a Ukrainian An-124 cargo aircraft.
Video footage broadcast by several German media outlets showed the plane on the runway with emergency vehicles next to it.
German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt cut his summer break short and returned to the country to address the incident. He said the armed drone found was a hybrid attack which opened a "new level of danger."
Addressing journalists who had gathered at the airport, Dobrindt said that people behind the incident would need to have a high level of technical expertise and experience in dealing with explosives. This spoke against "an amateurish approach," Dobrindt said.
"We are dealing here with a professional hybrid threat scenario," he added.
In another incident at the same airport on August 5, a DHL cargo aircraft reportedly collided midair with an unknown object shortly after takeoff from Leipzig, prompting an immediate unscheduled landing in Hanover.
The Leipzig/Halle airport is a major logistical hub for DHL, a German-owned international shipping giant.
DHL Crash
A DHL plane crashed near Vilnius in November 2024, killing the jet's Spanish pilot and injuring another Spanish crew member, a German, and a Lithuanian.
The crash came amid concerns among Western security officials that Russian intelligence is preparing acts of sabotage targeting Western cargo aircraft, though officials have said so far they have no evidence of a link.
In November 2025, the Safety Investigation Division of Lithuania's Justice Ministry said a report into the incident is expected in the coming months.
In July 2024, there were a series of fires at courier companies in Poland, the United Kingdom, and at the DHL freight center at the Leipzig/Halle Airport.
Lithuanian authorities have alleged the actions were organized and coordinated by people with links to Russia's military intelligence service. Moscow has denied any involvement in the incidents.
At a trial in Lithuania earlier this week, a DHL company representative told the court that the parcel caught fire on the ground at the logistics center shortly before loading, rather than during the flight, because the plane was delayed.
Five suspects are on trial in the case. The men, aged between 23 and 69, are accused of terrorist acts and forming an organized terrorist association. Lithuanian investigators allege the five were recruited by Russian agents to help deliver the packages to various locations for DHL to ship.

items.title: Russian Barrage On Kyiv Region Kills 17 Amid Ukraine's Air Defense Missile Shortage
items.summary: BROVARY, Ukraine -- Russian overnight drone and ballistic missile strikes killed at least 17 people in the Kyiv region, as Ukraine warned of critical air defense shortages and urged its allies to hasten deliveries of urgently needed air defense missiles.
items.body_text:
BROVARY, Ukraine -- Russian overnight drone and ballistic missile strikes killed at least 17 people in the Kyiv region, as Ukraine warned of critical air defense shortages and urged its allies to hasten deliveries of urgently needed air defense missiles.
"Russia has once again brought death and destruction to our land, taking the lives of civilians," Tymur Tkachenko, head of the Kyiv Regional State Administration, wrote on Telegram on August 5.
Tkachenko added that the highest death toll was recorded in the Brovary district, where 10 people were killed. Among the dead were eight people who had been waiting at a railway station for a delayed train.
In recent years, Russia has intensified its attacks on Ukraine's railway infrastructure, disrupting civilian routes and seeking to hinder the country's vital humanitarian and military shipments to frontline regions.
Reporting from the scene in Brovary, RFE/RL's Ukrainian Service captured shocking images showing bodies scattered across the station, as emergency workers were deployed to the site.
Russian strikes on August 5 also killed five people in the Bucha district and one person in the Fastiv district, Tkachenko said, while Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported that another person had been killed in the attack on the capital itself. At least 44 other people were injured.
Elsewhere, Russian strikes also targeted the Sumy, Zaporizhzhya, and Donetsk regions, killing at least four people.
The Ukrainian military said that Russia launched an attack on Ukraine using 24 ballistic missiles, four hypersonic missiles, and 115 drones, with the Kyiv region as the primary target.
It added in a separate statement that Ukrainian air defenses shot down or suppressed 98 Russian drones but intercepted none of the missiles launched, marking a rather rare occurrence in recent years.
The Russian Defense Ministry confirmed the attack on Kyiv and the surrounding area, saying it targeted transport, logistics, and distribution centers with precision weapons and long-range drones.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who has been pushing the United States and Kyiv's European allies in recent months to provide Ukraine with more air defense systems, said on X that "ballistic missile interceptors could have saved the lives of those killed today."
"It is very important that our partners understand that delays in supplying them, or an unwillingness to provide anti-ballistic systems, lead directly to such horrific casualties and destruction," he added.
Since the beginning of the year, Russia has managed to capture only a small amount of territory, marking a sharp slowdown compared with previous months. However, with Ukraine facing severe shortages of air defense systems capable of intercepting high-speed ballistic missiles, Moscow has stepped up its missile attacks.
Following the Russian attack on August 5, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced that the European Union is making a further 1.4 billion euros ($1.6 billion) available to Ukraine, using the proceeds from immobilized Russian assets, saying that "Russia must pay for the destruction it has caused."
"Once again, we wake up to the news of horrible atrocities committed by Russia through its aerial attacks on Ukraine," von der Leyen said. She added that new funds "will support Ukraine's continued resistance against Russia's illegal war."
Meanwhile, authorities in Russia's Tula region, which borders Moscow, reported that another facility belonging to Wildberries, the country's largest online retailer, had been hit by drones.
Images posted on social media showed thick plumes of black smoke rising from the facility. Ukrainian officials have not commented on the attack.
Kyiv has sought to disrupt Wildberries' operations in recent weeks, accusing the company of aiding Russia's war against Ukraine by supplying goods that have military purposes.

items.title: Sudan war threatens ancient Meroe pyramids, a UNESCO Heritage Site
items.summary: More than 200 ancient Meroe pyramids are imperilled by Sudan’s escalating war and neglect.
items.body_text:
In Pictures
Sudan war threatens ancient Meroe pyramids, a UNESCO Heritage Site
More than 200 ancient Meroe pyramids are imperilled by Sudan’s escalating war and neglect.
Sudan’s war is endangering the ancient pyramids of Meroe, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, as fighting and a lack of security have brought all preservation work to a halt and left the fragile structures exposed to the elements.
“The site may face a disaster, and collapses are possible,” archaeologist Mahmoud Suleiman said, warning that the more than three-year conflict has prevented experts from carrying out basic maintenance.
Located about 200km (125 miles) north of Khartoum, Meroe is home to more than 200 narrow, steep-sided pyramids built between 800 BC and 350 AD as tombs for rulers of the Kingdom of Kush.
Guards said windblown sand and encroaching vegetation are accelerating their decay. “The sand has thickened heavily on the pyramids and even inside the temples, and the grass grows thick,” guard Mustafa Ahmed said.
“The pyramids have deteriorated greatly, and stones have begun to fall.”
Antiquities inspector Mohamed Mubarak said salt released from accumulated sand is attacking the “inherently fragile” stones, eroding ancient inscriptions.
Suleiman said climate change, the dispersal of Sudan’s archaeological workforce and the halt of foreign missions have all contributed to “significant deterioration”.
UNESCO has warned that more than 100 cultural sites have been damaged and at least 22 museums looted or destroyed since the war began in April 2023.

US-Israel war on Iran upends Europe’s summer holiday travel patterns
Holidaymakers are sticking closer to home as the conflict rages, while tourism operators adapt.
London, United Kingdom – Nadia Waleed had set off from London with her husband and three daughters for a holiday in Bali, before continuing on to Pakistan, with stopovers in Dubai.
“A family holiday with multiple flights and stopovers is stressful at the best of times, but the situation in Iran resulted in multiple last minute changes in flight schedules by [the Emirates] airline,” she told Al Jazeera about her trip this summer.

- list 3 of 4Wildfires in Spain and France force evacuation of more than 267,000 people
- list 4 of 4Hindus take holy dip in India’s rivers on sacred holiday
Days before flying, her return flight schedule had changed. A three-hour stopover in Dubai was now extended to 18 hours.
“A two-hour-long phone marathon ensued whereby we managed to get earlier return flights from Pakistan which reduced the layover duration,” she said.
But the next day, one family member’s schedule was changed again – their return flight was pushed back by a month.
“We have also had emails informing us of changes in flight details during our holiday by one hour, requiring rearranging of taxis and pickups,” she said.
Her experience is a small, personal illustration of a larger disruption.
The United States-Israel war on Iran has forced airlines to abandon huge stretches of airspace, sending commercial traffic on longer, costlier detours and upending the plans of families, retirees and honeymooners.
At Trailfinders, a UK travel company, the shockwaves arrived in bulk.
“The Middle East conflict meant Trailfinders had thousands of bookings to rearrange or cancel,” said Nikki Davies of the agency, pointing to Dubai, Qatar and Abu Dhabi, destinations in their own right but also crucial transit points for travellers heading on to Australia and Asia.
Once the UK’s Foreign Office advised against travel to the region, which invalidated insurance if ignored, the clients postponed in droves.
That advisory has since been lifted, and Davies described “incredible pent-up demand” for travel through the Gulf again.
But the disruption appears to have shifted where people choose to travel to.
“Europe is proving extremely popular as it’s closer to home and the standout destinations are Italy, Spain, Greece and Norway,” she said.
TUI, Europe’s largest tour operator, is seeing the same shift at scale.
“Traditionally, 75 percent of the European travellers at TUI book their summer holidays in Europe,” said TUI spokesperson Aage Dunhaupt. “This trend for package holidays is even stronger this year and shows that holidaymakers flock to the all-inclusive and protected package holidays.”
‘Almost like COVID’
The European Union Aviation Safety Agency this week told airlines to avoid Jordanian airspace after renewed attacks, extending its existing warning against Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, the UAE and Oman until August 31.
British Airways has suspended flights to Dubai, Doha, Abu Dhabi and Tel Aviv, and will permanently drop its London-Jeddah route. Its twice-daily London-Riyadh service will be cut to once a day when it resumes in August. Virgin Atlantic has suspended its London-Dubai route through the coming winter season.
For independent travel agent Assra Satti, the anxiety showed up in the fine print. A family booking a July holiday to Vietnam via Istanbul wanted written guarantees before committing, wondering if they would be rerouted or reimbursed should the war disrupt their flights.
Satti secured written confirmation of both options, and the family flew as planned. As the holiday approached, the same clients expressed concern about a rumour circulating on social media that jet fuel surcharges might land them with an unex
