items.title: A Velencei-tó iszapjába süppedt egy nő, szolgálaton kívüli rendőr mentette ki
items.summary: A 35 éves nőt kórházba vitték.
items.body_text:
A Velencei-tó iszapjába süppedt egy nő, szolgálaton kívüli rendőr mentette ki
A Velencei-tó iszapjába ragadt egy 35 éves nő szerda késő este, ezért a segítségére kellett sietni – közölte a Fejér megyei rendőrség a Facebookon. Este tíz után jött a bejelentés a rendőrségre, hogy egy ember nem tud egyedül kijönni az iszapból.
A Gárdonyi Rendőrkapitányság egyik rendőre nem sokkal előtte végzett a szolgálattal, de hallotta a rádión a bejelentést. Hazafelé tartott, de úgy döntött, segít a bajba jutott nőnek. Odament a tóhoz, ahol egy másik ember segítségével kimentették a nőt a tómederből. Időközben más rendőrök és a mentők is kiérkeztek, a nőt kórházba vitték.
Július végén is történt egy hasonló eset, ekkor egy férfi át akart gyalogolni a Velencei-tavon, de ő is besüppedt az iszapba, a vízirendőröknek kellett kimenteniük. A rendőrség azt kérte, hogy senki ne próbáljon gyalogosan átkelni a tavon, még akkor sem, ha a víz sekélynek látszik.
Az előrejelzések szerint a Velencei-tó vízszintje augusztusra csupán 20 centiméteres lesz. A Velencei-tó vízpótlási lehetőségeiről és azok bonyolult ökológiai és műszaki problémáiról nemrég ezt a videót készítettük:

items.body_text:
"Ivan, Go Home!" Rally to Take Place Outside Russian Embassy in Prague
Prague Morning
A Czech-Ukrainian rally will take place outside the Russian Embassy in Prague on August 20 to mark the 58th anniversary of the Soviet-led invasion of Czechoslovakia.
The event, titled “Ivan, Go Home!”, is scheduled to begin at 6 p.m. on Thursday, August 20, at Boris Němcova Square in Prague 6.
The rally comes one day before the anniversary of the night of August 20-21, 1968, when troops from five Warsaw Pact countries entered Czechoslovakia to crush the Prague Spring reform movement.
The invasion brought an end to the country’s attempt to pursue a more liberal form of socialism and was followed by two decades of political repression and Soviet military presence.
The event is being organized jointly by People in Need (Člověk v tísni), Memory of the People (Paměť národa), Million Moments for Democracy (Milion chvilek pro demokracii), and the European Congress of Ukrainians.
Organizers say the rally will connect the historical experience of the Soviet occupation with Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine.
Participants will gather to remember those killed or persecuted following the 1968 invasion and the people who lived under the communist regime that followed. The organizers also plan to express support for Ukraine and draw attention to what they describe as the continuing use of imperial violence by Russia.
The choice of the rally’s name refers to one of the best-known slogans associated with the 1968 invasion. “Ivan, go home!” appeared on posters, walls, buildings and military vehicles as Czechoslovaks protested against the foreign troops occupying the country.
The invasion halted those reforms. Soviet troops remained in Czechoslovakia until the end of the communist era, while the subsequent period of “normalization” brought censorship, political purges and restrictions on civil liberties.

items.body_text:
World of Warcraft Film Ibelin to Shoot in Prague
Prague Morning
Production of Ibelin, a new film based on the life of Norwegian World of Warcraft player Mats Steen, is moving to Prague this summer.
Filming is expected to take place at Barrandov Studios from early August through early October, following the production’s spring shoot in Norway.
The film is not connected to the 2016 Hollywood movie Warcraft. Instead, it tells the real-life story of Steen, who lived with Duchenne muscular dystrophy and built friendships, relationships and a social life inside the online world of World of Warcraft.
The Prague production is reportedly seeking extras for roles including blacksmiths, guards and innkeepers. The casting suggests that parts of the film set in the game’s fictional world could be filmed in the Czech Republic. The producers have not yet officially confirmed which scenes will be shot in Prague.
Charlie Plummer leads the cast
American actor Charlie Plummer will portray Mats Steen. Toni Collette and Stephen Graham will play his parents, while the supporting cast includes Bill Nighy, Isabela Merced, Maisy Stella, John Bradley and Ivanna Sakhno.
The film will be directed by Norwegian filmmaker Morten Tyldum, whose credits include The Imitation Game and the science-fiction film Passengers.
At the center of the story is the difference between Steen’s increasingly restricted physical existence and the freedom he experienced online. His character, known in World of Warcraft as Ibelin, became an important figure to people he met through the game.
One of Norway’s largest film projects
The Prague shoot is part of an international production with a reported budget of CZK 1 billion.
According to the Norwegian Film Institute, the project received 20 million Norwegian kroner in production support.
Ibelin is being produced by Vendôme Pictures, Pathé and Neby-Tyldum as an international co-production. The Norwegian Film Institute describes it as an English-language drama with a planned running time of around two hours.
The film is being developed for theatrical release, with its premiere currently expected in the third quarter of 2027.

items.body_text:
GALLERY: Time Capsule Buried Beneath Prague's Wenceslas Square Tramline
Prague Morning
A time capsule containing different items, newspapers and messages documenting life in 2026 has been buried beneath Prague’s reconstructed Wenceslas Square.
The capsule was placed on Wednesday, August 5, near the statue of St. Wenceslas as work continues on the upper section of the square.
The Prague New Town Association, which is involved in activities around the statue and the surrounding area, organised the ceremony.
The date was not originally chosen for its historical significance. Construction work ultimately determined both the day and the location of the burial. But the association later discovered that August 5 also marks the 60th anniversary of the release of the Beatles’ Revolver album.
“We were wondering what made August 5 go down in history. Then we found out that it was 60 years ago that the Beatles released their famous album Revolver. So now we are leaving a message here for future generations,” said Monika Vlková, the association’s executive director.
The box, measuring 60 by 40 by 23.5 centimetres and weighing about eight kilograms, was then taken to a prepared pit beside the statue. Workers had excavated the hole to a depth of around 1.7 metres, where the capsule was placed before the site was covered.
The container had been wrapped in transparent protective film, as had its contents.
The collection includes coins, newspapers published during the first week of August 2026, T-shirts, badges and written messages. It also contains proposals submitted by architects during the competition for the redesign of Wenceslas Square.
The box reportedly also holds a hammer and a beer glass.
The objects are accompanied by a 20-page report describing everyday life in the Czech capital in 2026. The capsule also contains USB drives with digital material documenting the period of the Covid-19 pandemic and its effects on life in central Prague.
The capsule is intended to remain underground for decades. The association estimates that Wenceslas Square could undergo another major reconstruction in roughly 50 years, although nobody can predict when the next intervention will actually take place.

items.body_text:
Two Minor Girls Arrested as Giga Avaliani Case Widens
Two teenage girls, Nia Imnadze and Anastasia Beruashvili, were arrested late on August 5 as the prosecution further expanded the circle of minors implicated in the high-profile murder case of 28-year-old tutor Giga Avaliani, who died after spending three weeks in a coma following an assault near his apartment block in Tbilisi in October 2025.
Imnadze, reportedly 16, was arrested at her family’s apartment in a highly emotional scene. In a video captured by her lawyer, her parents are seen verbally confronting police officers as they dispute the allegations against their daughter, while officers said they were acting on a court order. Imnadze was reportedly hospitalized shortly afterward and transferred to a temporary detention cell the following afternoon.
Imnadze and Beruashvili are reportedly the girlfriends of Aleksandre Gabashvili and Giorgi Rikadze, respectively, two of the main defendants in Avaliani’s case, who were sentenced in April to 14 years in prison each after being found guilty of “intentional infliction of serious harm to health resulting in death.” As they were minors at the time of the crime, their sentences were automatically reduced to ten years and six months.
According to media reports, Imnadze faces a charge of “abetting intentional infliction of serious harm to health by a group” under Article 25-117 of Georgia’s Criminal Code. Avaliani’s family has long identified Imnadze, who was his pupil, as one of the central figures in the case, alleging that she encouraged her boyfriend to assault him.
Beruashvili, meanwhile, faces a charge of “failure to report a particularly serious crime” under Article 376.
Five minors in the case have already been sentenced to multiple years in prison, while several more, including the son of former Deputy Interior Minister Merab Malania, remain on trial. The widening of the prosecution follows months-long efforts by Avaliani’s mother, Eka Kupatadze, to hold everyone she believes responsible for her son’s death accountable.
“Georgia has won another battle against the murderers of Giga Avaliani, a healthy, innocent, genius young doctor!” Kupatadze wrote on Facebook following the latest arrests.
Both girls’ families have reportedly rejected the allegations, while their lawyers have described the charges as “absurd.”

items.body_text:
Nationwide Blackout Hits Georgia Third Time in Two Weeks
Georgia was hit by another nationwide power blackout on the evening of August 5, the third such incident in two weeks following the July 24–25 outages.
Power was cut at around 20:10, forcing Tbilisi Metro, among other services, to stop operating, while individual consumers across the country were reporting the outage on social media. Electricity began to be gradually restored from around 21:00.
Giorgi Pangani, a member of Georgia’s National Energy and Water Supply Regulatory Commission (GNERC), which acts as an independent regulator overseeing the electricity sector, said the outage occurred during “planned testing” by State Electrosystem (GSE), the country’s main transmission grid owner, at units of Enguri HPP, a major electricity producer to Georgia, including the occupied Abkhazia region.
GSE later issued a statement saying that the work at Enguri HPP was aimed at studying the causes of the July 24–25 blackouts and required the electricity system to operate in isolation and at non-standard frequencies, resulting in the temporary nationwide outage.
GSE Head Vano Zardiashvili was reported to have been dismissed days after the July 24–25 outages.

items.body_text:
Hungarian Journalist László Róbert Mézes Detained by Migration Officials in Tbilisi
László Róbert Mézes, a Hungarian journalist who has lived in Georgia and covered anti-government protests, has been detained by the officers of the Interior Ministry’s Migration Department and may face expulsion.
His lawyer Tornike Janelidze confirmed the detention to several Georgian media outlets on the evening of August 5. While the lawyer is expected to provide more details after the in-person meeting with the detainee, the Interior Ministry told Civil.ge that he was in Georgia “without legal grounds” and had overstayed his permitted period of stay.
The ministry added that Mézes is being detained under Article 64-2-b of Georgia’s Law on the Legal Status of Aliens and Stateless Persons. According to the provision, “aliens may be detained and placed in temporary holding facilities or temporary accommodation centres for their expulsion” if “there is a risk of absconding by the alien.”
The detention was first reported by Georgian lawyer Marika Arevadze, who said that Mézes has been staying legally in Georgia.
The journalist, who has earlier also contributed to Civil.ge, has actively covered the anti-government protests in Georgia. He has been a fierce critic of former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán.
More to follow…

items.title: US funding for TRIPP+ Enterprise, including Trump Route project, doubles to more than $400 million
items.summary: The spending boost follows reports that Russia-born businessperson Konstantin Sokolov was appointed to ‘oversee' the fund.
items.body_text:
US funding for TRIPP+ Enterprise, including Trump Route project, doubles to more than $400 million
The US government’s official spending database shows that money allocated for TRIPP+ Enterprise Fund, the parent funding source of the Trump Route, has increased from $201 million to $402 million. The implementation deadline has remained untouched, and the US has yet to officially comment on the funding boost.
The Trump Route, also known by its official name the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP), agreed upon by Armenia and Azerbaijan with US mediation, would connect Azerbaijan to its exclave Nakhchivan through Armenian territory.
The initial funding was approved in January 2026 by the State Department with an implementation period of approximately 10 years. Although there is not yet an official statement about the increase, the database shows that on 16 July, the funding was doubled.
The enterprise fund is separate from the TRIPP Development Company, which is a joint venture between the US and Armenia, where the US holds a 74% stake while Armenia holds the remaining 26%. Earlier it was reported that Konstantin Sokolov, a Russia-born businessperson based in the US, and one of the donors to President Donald Trump’s unfinished $350 million White House ballroom project, has been appointed to ‘oversee’ the fund.
The project is part of Washington’s broader push for economic influence in the region. The Trump Route is a central part of the newfound US engagement in the South Caucasus and a key outcome of the 2025 Washington meeting between Trump, Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan, and Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev. The historic talks resulted in the initialling, but not the signing, of a peace treaty between Armenia and Azerbaijan, as well as laying the basis for the Trump Route.

items.title: Azerbaijan arrests 9 TikTokers for ‘immoral behaviour’
items.summary: The content creators were arrested over a period of two weeks in July and early August.
items.body_text:
Azerbaijan intensified its arrest of local TikTokers in July, accusing them of violating moral values on social media — an act criminalised under Azerbaijan’s administrative offences code in early 2026.
On 2 August, 35-year-old TikToker Alikram Heydarov was sentenced to eight days in jail under charges of hooliganism.
The pro-government media outlet Unikal reported that he was arrested for ‘demonstrating disrespect toward society and engaging in unethical behaviour’ on social media, and was charged with hooliganism for violating public order and demonstrating a ‘clear disrespect for society’.
Heydarov has 79.3K followers and 1.8 million likes on TikTok. His content primarily focuses on his day-to-day life. However, he recently posted a video in which he criticised people for not accepting Shia Muslims.
The day prior, 39-year-old TikToker Sanur Azizov was jailed by order of the Sabail District Court under the same charge for eight days.
On 30 July, Muzhgan Mammadzada, another TikTok vlogger, was sentenced to 10 days, with Unikal claimed that she jailed for ‘engaging in acts that offend public morality and openly express disrespect for society’ and specifically ‘immoral expressions, making gestures that convey such content, or displaying parts of the human body in a manner contrary to moral norms and to national and spiritual values’.
On the same day as Mammadzada’s arrest, another TikTok user, 39-year-old Murad Gasimov, was jailed allegedly ‘for showing disrespect toward society and for posting material on social media that demonstrated unethical behavior and contradicted moral values’. He was sentenced to one month in prison.
On 29 July, 43-year old TikToker user Sakina Ahmadova was placed under 10 days of administrative arrest allegedly for publishing ‘information the dissemination of which is prohibited, as well as for failing to take measures to prevent the posting of such information’.
According to Unikal, Magsad Baghirov, who is known ‘for sharing anti-religious calls’ on social media, was also sentenced to 10 days in late July.
Separately, pro-government media outlet Okhu.az reported that three TikTokers aged between 20 and 24 were handed eight day sentences each for ‘disturbing public peace and inconveniencing citizens’ by shooting in public.
The wave of arrests against TikTokers began in April 2024. At the time, the Interior Ministry told OC Media that dozens of content creators had been arrested for creating ‘immoral content’.
In December 2025, parliament discussed the amendments that classified ‘immoral activity on social media directed against society and the national morality’ as petty hooliganism. These amendments were signed into law by President Ilham Aliyev in January 2026.
Human rights lawyer Yalchin Imanov told OC Media that the new rules do not provide a clear definition of what exactly constitutes ‘immoral activity’ that contradicts accepted values.
He stressed that they will contribute to the strengthening of the government’s control over society and self-censorship on social media.

items.title: Conflict erupts at Lamaria Monastery in Georgia’s Ushguli over unauthorised construction
items.summary: The conflict erupted between locals and clergy over illegal constructions at the 10th century monastery.
items.body_text:
A dispute over an unauthorised construction at the historic Lamaria Monastery in Georgia’s Svaneti region has sparked a conflict between clergy and local residents. The Diocese of Mestia and Zemo Svaneti has said that nuns were subjected to verbal abuse and threats over the dispute.
The dispute concerns the construction of residential quarters on the grounds of the Lamaria Monastery, a UNESCO World Heritage site in Ushghuli, Svaneti. Although the work has since been halted on the orders of the National Agency for Cultural Heritage Protection, disagreements surrounding the site have continued.
Residents interviewed by OC Media said the dispute was linked to the construction rather than opposition to religious services themselves.
The issue gained public attention after independent media outlet Chai Khana reported on 8 July that construction of a refectory and residential cells had been underway near the monastery for more than a month without the required permits.
Following the report, the National Agency for Cultural Heritage Protection said the works were being carried out without its approval. The agency said Georgian legislation requires prior authorisation for any construction, rehabilitation, or other intervention at protected cultural heritage sites.
The agency later announced that the construction had been halted and said it was examining the case in accordance with legal procedures.
After OC Media contacted the National Agency for Cultural Heritage Protection on Wednesday, the agency confirmed that the construction remained suspended.
Diocese claims nuns abandoned monastery after local aggression
On Tuesday, the Diocese of Mestia and Zemo Svaneti issued a statement rejecting reports that the monastery had been locked by the local priest and closed to visitors.
The Diocese said the monastery’s nuns left after ‘a group of about 12–15 people’ came to the convent and subjected clergy and nuns to verbal abuse, threats, and aggressive behaviour.
It said members of the group told the clergy that ‘after your arrival, the situation in the village has worsened’, that the nuns were ‘desecrating the place’, and that they should leave the monastery.
The Diocese said the monastery’s keys were handed over to local residents after the nuns departed.
It added that monastic life and regular religious services would resume if villagers submitted a written request expressing support, saying this would help establish whether there was a shared position within the community.
Nato Subari, a schoolteacher from Chuberi, Svaneti, said local concerns centred on preserving the authenticity of the centuries-old monastery and preventing new buildings from being erected within the protected heritage site.
Subari added, however, that the controversy had also revealed differing views within the community.
She said some residents support maintaining an active monastery with regular Orthodox services, while others believe the complex should primarily be preserved as a historical monument and oppose further construction within its grounds.
‘There is no talk of stopping services in the village’, Subari told OC Media. ‘Everyone wants services to continue — people simply do not want these cells to be built’.
She also noted that, under local tradition, the keys to some churches in Svaneti are occasionally entrusted to nearby residents when clergy are absent.
The Lamaria Monastery, located above the village of Zhibiani, is a cultural heritage site dating back to the 9th and 10th centuries. The Diocese of Mestia and Zemo Svaneti says that, following the establishment of the diocese in 2002, ‘many previously closed churches were opened, regular divine services were restored, and a revival of spiritual life began throughout the diocese’.
The Lamaria Monastery is one of upper Svaneti’s most famous medieval religious monuments and is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
While the construction has been halted, the controversy appears to have deepened divisions within Ushg

items.title: Yle survey: Finns Party support edges up — opposition SDP widens gap with government's NCP
items.summary: The SDP held its position as the country's most popular party.
items.body_text:
Parts of the article content might not be accessible, for example, with a screen reader.
The Finns Party saw the biggest gains in Yle's latest party support survey, published on Thursday.
The opposition Left Alliance saw the largest drop in support, while support for the Centre Party also declined.
The opposition SDP held its position as the country's most popular party, according to the survey.
Support for the Finns Party rose to 15.6 percent in the August survey, a level it last reached in October 2024.
During the polling period — between 6 July and 3 August — the Finns Party's Social Affairs and Health Minister Wille Rydman's funding decisions sparked political debate.
Tens of thousands of migrants arriving in the Spanish territory of Ceuta also dominated discussion towards the end of the polling period. Interior Minister Mari Rantanen (Finns) demanded Spain's expulsion from the Schengen area. The minister later conceded that the country cannot be excluded from the visa-free zone simply because a member state demands it, and ministers said Rantanen's comment did not reflect the government's policy.
However, the Finns Party's support already started showing signs of recovery in Yle's poll in July.
According to Taloustutkimus research chief Tuomo Turja, the Finns Party gained new supporters primarily from the Centre Party and the National Coalition.
Political debate during the polling period may have appealed particularly to people on the far end of other right-leaning parties, Turja suggested. He said Finance Minister Riikka Purra's Finns Party appears to be attracting new supporters from higher income brackets.
"The Finns Party gains supporters fairly evenly from men and women. The biggest factor in the rise has been older people — over-50s — switching from the Centre Party to the Finns."
SDP widens gap
The largest opposition party, SDP, maintained its first-place position with 23.8 percent support, up 0.6 percentage points. It leads the second-place NCP by 6.8 percent. Turja said that gap is relatively large but not exceptional, and the figures typically narrow as elections approach.
The Greens also gained support, rising 0.4 percentage points to nine percent. Support for the one-MP Movement Now party exceeded two percent for the first time since the last election.
Left Alliance support drops sharply
The Left Alliance suffered the biggest fall, dropping 1.1 percentage points to 10.3 percent. Turja said the party is no longer attracting supporters from other red-green bloc parties — the Greens and SDP — as it typically does.
He said that voters are simply redistributing themselves among those three parties. The Left Alliance has lost support where the Greens have gained, particularly among urban women and young adults.
Support for the Centre Party, in fourth place, also dropped significantly — 0.9 percentage points to 12.7 percent. The Centre has steadily lost supporters to the three largest parties and to non-voters.
As recently as the spring, the Centre was in tight competition with the Finns Party for third place.
"Now it looks like these parties' trajectories are headed in quite different directions," Turja said.
According to Turja, the Garden Helsinki funding controversy chipped away at the National Coalition's support, which fell to 17 percent.
Despite the turbulence, the Finns Party's growth pushed the government parties' combined support slightly higher to 39.8 percent.
Taloustutkimus interviewed 2,125 adults in mainland Finland between 6 July and 3 August, with 76 percent of respondents indicating which party they would vote for if parliamentary elections were held now. The margin of error was 2.2 percentage points in either direction.

items.summary: The rain on Thursday is expected to head northeast, affecting areas from central Finland to southern Lapland. Thunderstorms are possible in some areas.
items.body_text:
A precipitation system is approaching Finland from the southwest on Thursday, according to Yle meteorologist Elias Paakkanen.
The rain is expected to head northeast, affecting areas from central Finland to southern Lapland. Thunderstorms are possible in some areas.
Temperatures will remain relatively cool in northern rainy areas.
At the same time, southern areas are expected to see dry and sunny weather, with higher temperatures.
Local showers are forecast on Friday, as a low pressure system moves eastward, with rainy conditions mainly affecting eastern and northern areas.
The rest of the country is expected to be mostly dry but fairly cloudy on Friday. But it will likely be sunny in the south, southwest and northern Lapland.

items.title: Sweden's inflation rate plummets in July
items.summary: Inflation according to the CPIF measure fell to 0.7 percent in July, according to preliminary figures from Statistics Sweden.
items.body_text:
CPIF inflation fell to 0.7 percent in July, according to preliminary figures from Statistics Sweden (SCB).
"The fact that inflation is now falling is largely due to tax cuts," said Susanne Spector, chief economist at Danske Bank.
The fall is in line with expectations. Analysts had on average expected inflation to fall to 0.7 percent.
The new figure can be compared with 1.3 percent inflation in June.
"Energy prices fell sharply in July, which contributed to the lower inflation rate according to the CPI and CPIF," said Mikael Nordin, price statistician at SCB.
The unusually low inflation is influenced by, among other things, the temporary tax cut on fuel and the temporary government subsidy for monthly public transport passes that was introduced on July 1st.
"Inflationary pressure is low and highly dependent on the government's tax policy. Excluding this, it would have been closer to the inflation target of 2 percent," said Susanne Spector, chief economist at Danske Bank.
However, inflation is not so low that there is reason for the Riksbank to lower the interest rate, she said.
The inflation rate measured as the CPI fell to 0.2 percent, a decline from 0.7 percent in June.
The Riksbank's inflation target is a CPIF inflation rate of 2.0 percent. CPIF inflation rate refers to an inflation rate where the effects of mortgage interest have been removed.

Hedgehogs mysteriously disappearing
Next week the third annual hedgehog count begins in Sweden. The survey has previously shown that the animal is no longer sighted in several places where they should be.
In 2024, 50,000 hedgehogs were reported, last year 55,000. WWF and Nordens Ark now want to hear from the public about as many sightings of hedgehogs – both alive and dead – as possible.
According to Jessica Ångström at WWF, the hedgehog is an endangered animal whose endangered status is getting worse and worse. This could be due to traffic, lost habitats or diseases, parasites, and/or environmental toxins.
Last year's data showed that the animal seems to be missing from several areas in Sweden where it was previously found – e.g. areas around Gothenburg, Bohuslän and Dalsland, and north of Stockholm up towards Uppsala.
"There seem to be a shortage of them there and we can't really answer why right now," said Ångström.
Hedgehog Week occurs in week 33, this year 10–16 August, for the third year in a row. The project is run by WWF and Nordens Ark and will last for at least five years. Funding comes from the Swedish Postcode Lottery.

items.title: The app helping Berliners track ticket inspections on public transport
items.summary: A community-driven app allows Berlin public transport users to share live alerts about fare inspections across the city's train and tram network.
items.body_text:
A new Berlin-based app, FreiFahren, enables public transport users to share and view real-time reports of ticket inspections across much of Berlin's public transport network.
Developed by the citizens’ initiative FreiFahren e.V., the service displays reported inspections on a map and uses recent reports to highlight routes where checks may be more likely.
According to its founders, the project is about more than avoiding inspectors. They argue that rising ticket prices and penalties for fare evasion disproportionately affect people on low incomes and that access to transport shouldn’t be a privilege.
In support of its argument, the initiative points to claims that up to 9,000 people are imprisoned in Germany each year for travelling without a valid ticket.
READ ALSO: How you could end up in a German prison if you're caught without a transport ticket
How the App works
Using FreiFahren is straightforward. When a user sees ticket inspectors on Berlin’s U-Bahn, S-Bahn or tram network, they can submit a report through the app. Reports include the station, line and direction of travel, and appear on a live map that refreshes every few seconds.
The system relies primarily on user-generated reports, although information can also come from linked Telegram groups, where a bot extracts relevant details from messages.
According to the founders, around 40,000 people use the app regularly with about 100 users active at any given time on average. But the app offers no guarantees against being caught.
Passengers are required to have valid ticket before boarding U Bahns, S Bahns, trams or buses in Berlin.
In addition to individual reports, the app displays a colour-coded risk model indicating where inspections may be more likely based on activity during the previous hour.
FreiFahren currently covers Berlin’s BVG network and the S-Bahn, including the underground, suburban rail and tram systems. Buses are not included.
The service is free to use and does not require registration. A web version is available and can be added to a phone’s home screen. Native iOS apps are available through Apple’s App Store, but an Android app is not yet available.
What are the legal and ethical implications?
Legally, FreiFahren appears to operate in a relatively secure position. Co-founder Johan Trieloff told taz that the organisation had sought legal advice and been informed there was "little room for legal action".
He compared inspection alerts to speed-camera warnings, which are widely available through other channels.
The ethical debate is less straightforward.
Public transport relies on fares and that helping people avoid inspections could undermine the system.
READ ALSO: What's the best option when buying public transport tickets in Berlin?
Trieloff rejects that position. He argues that the real issue is the criminalisation of people who cannot afford tickets, and says the app is intended to support people in precarious financial circumstances who still need to travel to work, appointments or other parts of daily life.
In his interview with taz, he argued that Berlin's inspection regime amounts to a system that "actively hunts" vulnerable people, rather than addressing the underlying causes of poverty and social exclusion.
Trieloff also speculated that transport operators might actually have little reason to oppose the app.
Citing anecdotal feedback from users, he said that many people who can afford tickets are more likely to buy one after seeing reports of nearby inspections.

items.title: Bavaria to introduce 'tap in' ticketing system for public transport
items.summary: Travel in Bavaria will look a little different from next year. The southern state plans to expand a tap-in/tap-out ticketing system for public transport.
items.body_text:
The Bavarian state government plans to gradually roll out the smartphone-based tap in/tap out ticketing system across the public transport network from the beginning of 2027.
The aim is to simplify ticket purchasing and automatically calculate fares for passengers.
According to the transport ministry in Bavaria, travellers will use a mobile app to check in before boarding a bus, the U-Bahn or train and check out when they reach their destination.
The system will then automatically determine the correct fare, removing the need for passengers to manually buy the correct ticket.
It is hoped that the system will work across different regional transport networks, allowing passengers to travel easily across the state.
Similar technology is already in place in some regions of Bavaria, including Munich's transport network. There, the process is known as "swiping" and requires that passengers swipe on a smartphone screen to begin and end a journey.
No plans for a 'Bayern Ticket'
The state government said it had abandoned the idea of a standardised ticketing and fare system across Bavaria.
According to the transport ministry, the Deutschlandticket – a nationwide travel pass that allows people to use public transport across Germany for €63 per month – is now the key priority.
Criticism has come from the Greens in the state parliament. Mobility spokesperson Markus Büchler said he regretted that the 'Bayern-Ticket' is not to be developed further.
"Resting on the laurels of the Deutschlandticket is not enough," he said. "Attractive offers must finally be created, particularly for people who only travel by bus and train occasionally."
In the Greens’ view, buying tickets must also be made easier and the fare system clearer. Furthermore, all regions of Bavaria should be connected to efficient transport networks. There are still gaps, particularly in Swabia and Lower Bavaria, Büchler said, adding that modern public transport "is not really feasible without an integrated network".
Unlike many other countries, Germany has no ticket barriers at transport stations. Instead, it uses an 'open-door honesty' system with random ticket checks.

items.body_text:
Thursday's top story: Explosive drone at German airport 'a new level of danger': minister
German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt has described the discovery of an explosive-laden drone at Leipzig-Halle Airport as a “professional hybrid threat scenario” that represents a new level of danger.
Authorities found, defused and later destroyed the drone after it was discovered near a Ukrainian-flagged cargo aircraft at the airport.
Dobrindt said investigators were examining the drone’s construction, the explosives used, its origin and any individuals or organisations potentially responsible. He stressed that the incident did not appear to be the work of amateurs and suggested that foreign actors could be among the possible sources of the threat, although investigations remain ongoing.
The discovery caused significant disruption at the airport, forcing the diversion of numerous flights.
In a separate incident, an aircraft that had aborted its landing reportedly collided with an unidentified object several kilometres away but was able to land safely.
Leipzig-Halle Airport is strategically important, serving military transport operations for Germany and its NATO allies, while also functioning as a base for Ukraine’s Antonov Airlines.
READ ALSO: UPDATE - Alarm at Leipzig airport after drone found carrying explosives
Berlin marks 65th anniversary of Wall construction with public installation
Berlin will commemorate the 65th anniversary of the beginning of the Berlin Wall’s construction with a temporary installation and open-air exhibition near the Brandenburg Gate.
Organised by the Berlin Wall Foundation, the commemorations will run from August 13th to 16th.
A 30-metre-long, almost three-metre-high structure designed to resemble the Berlin Wall will be erected close to the Brandenburg Gate. Alongside it, the exhibition Mauerblicke: Berlin 1961–1990 will use historical photographs to document the progressive closure of the city and the experiences of Berliners living under division.
Photo: picture alliance/dpa | Britta Pedersen
The anniversary programme will also include discussions with eyewitnesses, guided tours, concerts and readings across the city.
Full details are due to be announced on August 12th, one day before the anniversary of August 13th, 1961, when the East German government sealed the border with West Berlin.
Number of BAföG recipients falls to lowest level in more than a decade
The number of people receiving BAföG student support in Germany declined again in 2025, highlighting ongoing concerns about the effectiveness of the country’s main student aid scheme.
According to the Federal Statistics Office, 570,000 people received BAföG benefits last year, seven percent fewer than in 2024 and well below the 2012 peak of almost 980,000 recipients.
The findings come as the federal government delays parts of a planned reform, including an increase in the housing allowance for students, which will now take effect later than originally intended.

The German Student Services Organisation criticised the current system, arguing that BAföG reaches too few students and fails to provide sufficient support.
It also highlighted that many eligible students do not apply, calling for reforms and improved access to information about available financial assistance.

A major emergency response was launched at a hotel in Iserlohn, North Rhine-Westphalia, after a strong odour in a room and reports of respiratory irritation raised concerns about a hazardous substance.
Fire and rescue services detected elevated levels of ammonia, prompting some responders to wear chemical protection suits while investigating the incident.

She also highlighted Surabaya's role as Indonesia's maritime hub, noting that the city is home to the Naval Academy, the headquarters of the navy’s Marine Corps, Fleet Command II, Naval Regional Command V, and state-owned shipbuilder PT PAL Indonesia.
Apart from industrial and shipbuilding cooperation, the meeting also touched on the legacy of Cheng Ho, the Ming dynasty admiral and diplomat renowned for his voyages across Asia, including Indonesia, where he is widely recognized as a Chinese Muslim admiral.
Meanwhile, Chinese Consul General in Surabaya Ye Su said the visit marked the Chinese navy's second since 2023, reflecting the lasting friendship between the two countries.
He also commended Khofifah for advancing East Java's economy, investment, and sociocultural development.

items.title: Indonesia, EU target Q4 2026 signing for IEU-CEPA trade deal
items.summary: Indonesia and the European Union are on track to officially sign the long-awaited Indonesia-EU Comprehensive Economic ...
items.body_text:
The announcement was made by Indonesian Ministry of Trade’s Director of Bilateral Negotiations Basaria Tiara Desika L. Gaol in Jakarta on Wednesday (August 5), as the bilateral pact is entering its final administrative stages.
"We are targeting the signing of the agreement in the fourth quarter of 2026," Tiara noted.
The agreement reached a substantial conclusion in September 2025 during its 19th negotiation round in Bali, where Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs Airlangga Hartarto substantially agreed to the framework.
With the subsequent legal scrubbing process officially complete, both parties are preparing for final signature and legislative approval.
"The signing will be carried out by ministers from both parties, witnessed by the highest leaders from both the EU and Indonesia. After that, we will enter the ratification process," Tiara added.
The Indonesian government hopes the ratification process moves swiftly, allowing full implementation of IEU-CEPA by the first quarter of 2027 to deliver immediate economic benefits to the business sector.
Secretary of the Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs Susiwijono Moegiarso confirmed that the deal is projected to officially enter into force on January 1, 2027.
The implementation of the IEU-CEPA, he stressed, will open broader market access for Indonesian products and boost overall competitiveness against regional peers.
Susiwijono urged domestic industries—particularly manufacturing—to capitalize on the momentum to spur national economic growth.
First launched in Brussels in September 2016, negotiations for the IEU-CEPA have spanned nearly ten years.
Under the agreement, the EU will eliminate import duties on 98.5 percent of tariff lines, simplify procedures for Indonesian exports, and create greater investment opportunities in strategic sectors such as electric vehicles, electronics and pharmaceuticals.

items.title: Hasil Babak Pertama Persija vs Arema FC: Witan Cetak Gol, VAR Gagalkan Comeback Singo Edan
items.summary: Persija dan Arema bermain imbang 1-1 pada babak pertama perebutan tempat ketiga Piala Presiden 2026. Gol Arema sempat dianulir VAR karena handsball.
items.body_text:
Piala Presiden 2026
Hasil Babak Pertama Persija vs Arema FC: Witan Cetak Gol, VAR Gagalkan Comeback Singo Edan
Persija dan Arema bermain imbang 1-1 pada babak pertama perebutan tempat ketiga Piala Presiden 2026. Gol Arema sempat dianulir VAR karena handsball.
Ringkasan Berita:
- Persija Jakarta dan Arema FC bermain imbang 1-1 pada babak pertama perebutan tempat ketiga Piala Presiden 2026. Witan Sulaeman membawa Persija unggul, sebelum Salim Tuharea menyamakan kedudukan.
- Arema FC tampil lebih dominan dengan pressing tinggi. Namun efektivitas penyelesaian akhir masih menjadi kendala bagi tim asuhan Marcos Santos.
- Arema sempat membalikkan keadaan lewat gol Marcus Vinicius pada menit ke-40. Namun, VAR menganulir gol tersebut karena lebih dulu terjadi handsball.
TRIBUNNEWS.COM - Persija Jakarta dan Arema FC bertarung sengit dalam babak pertama perebutan posisi ketiga Piala Presiden 2026, Kamis (6/8/2026) sore WIB.
Berlangsung di Stadion Kapten I Wayan Dipta, Gianyar, duel babak pertama Persija vs Arema FC sementara ini berkedudukan imbang 1-1.
Persija Jakarta berhasil unggul lebih dulu melalui aksi Witan Sulaeman pada menit ke-7.
Sementara Arema mampu menyamakan kedudukan pada menit ke-28 melalui Salim Tuharea setelah memanfaatkan kemelut di mulut gawang Persija.
Arema FC sejatinya mampu berbalik unggul pada menit ke-40 melalui sepakan Marcus Vinicius. Namun gol tersebut dianulir VAR karena terdapat pemain Arema yang handsball lebih dulu sebelum terjadi gol.
Sepanjang empat puluh lima menit babak pertama ini, Arema FC bermain lebih dominan dengan pressing tinggi dan serangan cepatnya. Namun sayangnya penyelesaian di lini depan kurang klinis.
Sementara itu, Persija di bawah asuhan Shin Tae-yong menerapkan strategi menunggu sembari melakukan counter attack saat Arema kehilangan bola.
Baca juga: Pertaruhan Harga Diri Persija vs Arema FC sebelum Cabut dari Piala Presiden 2026
Jalannya Pertama
Arema FC langsung menerapkan tempo permainan tinggi sejak peluit babak pertama dibunyikan.
Tim berjuluk Singo Edan itu langsung mengancam dari sisi kanan melalui umpan silang , namun masih mampi diantisipasi kiper muda Persija, Hafizh Rizkianur.
Sejauk lima menit jalannya awal babak pertama, Arema FC memang cukup mendominasi namun belum mampu menciptakan peluang.
Persija Jakarta justru berhasil mencetak gol lebih dulu pada menit ke-7 saat umpan trobosan Fajar Fathurrahman dari sisi kanan mampu diselesaikan Witan Sulaeman ke arah tiang dekat.
Gol, Persija unggul 1-0.
Tersengat gol cepat, Arema FC pun mencoba membangun kembali dominasi serangannya.
Gustavo Franca mencoba melepaskan tembakan spekulasi dari luar kotak penalti pada menit ke-12, namun arahnya masih melebar tipis di samping gawang Hafizh.
Hingga menit ke-25, Arema FC pun cukup mendominasi dengan pressing tinggi yang baik terbukti beberapa kali mampu mencuri bola dari pemain Persija. Namun penyelesaiannya kurang klinis.

items.title: Marifit Jadi Pilihan Nutrisi Pendamping Harian, Bantu Jaga Metabolisme di Tengah Gaya Hidup Modern
items.summary: Dokter, apoteker, dan ahli gizi merekomendasikan Marifit sebagai nutrisi pendamping harian untuk membantu menjaga metabolisme tubuh
items.body_text:
Marifit Jadi Pilihan Nutrisi Pendamping Harian, Bantu Jaga Metabolisme di Tengah Gaya Hidup Modern
Dokter, apoteker, dan ahli gizi merekomendasikan Marifit sebagai nutrisi pendamping harian untuk membantu menjaga metabolisme tubuh
TRIBUNNEWS.COM – Gaya hidup modern membuat masyarakat semakin akrab dengan berbagai kebiasaan yang dapat memengaruhi kesehatan metabolisme, mulai dari konsumsi makanan tinggi gula dan lemak, pola makan yang tidak teratur, kurang tidur, minim aktivitas fisik, terlalu lama duduk, hingga stres berkepanjangan.
Jika berlangsung terus-menerus, kebiasaan tersebut dapat meningkatkan risiko terjadinya ketidakseimbangan metabolik yang berkaitan dengan kadar gula darah, tekanan darah, maupun kolesterol.
Kondisi ini membuat semakin banyak masyarakat menyadari bahwa menjaga metabolisme tidak hanya berkaitan dengan berat badan, tetapi juga penting untuk membantu tubuh mengubah makanan menjadi energi, menjaga fungsi organ, serta mendukung daya tahan tubuh agar tetap optimal.
Menurut Dr. Akhmad Haidar An Nuridy, menjaga metabolisme tubuh perlu dilakukan secara konsisten melalui penerapan pola hidup sehat yang dibarengi pemenuhan kebutuhan nutrisi.
"Metabolisme merupakan proses alami yang berlangsung setiap saat di dalam tubuh. Oleh karena itu, menjaganya tidak cukup dilakukan sesekali, tetapi harus menjadi bagian dari kebiasaan sehari-hari melalui pola makan bergizi seimbang, aktivitas fisik yang cukup, istirahat berkualitas, serta dukungan nutrisi yang tepat," ujarnya.
Selain menerapkan pola hidup sehat, pemenuhan nutrisi harian dinilai menjadi salah satu faktor yang membantu mendukung berbagai proses metabolisme tubuh. Vitamin, mineral, antioksidan, dan senyawa fitokimia dibutuhkan tubuh untuk menunjang berbagai fungsi fisiologis sekaligus membantu tubuh beradaptasi terhadap tantangan gaya hidup modern.
Menjawab kebutuhan tersebut, Marifit hadir sebagai nutrisi pendamping harian berbahan alami yang memadukan ekstrak daun kelor (Moringa oleifera) dan daun bidara.
Kedua bahan alami tersebut dikenal mengandung vitamin, mineral, antioksidan, serta berbagai senyawa fitokimia yang membantu mendukung metabolisme tubuh, menjaga daya tahan tubuh, dan membantu melindungi tubuh dari paparan radikal bebas sebagai bagian dari pola hidup sehat.
Kepercayaan terhadap Marifit juga diperkuat melalui ulasan dari sejumlah tenaga kesehatan, di antaranya Dr. Akhmad Haidar An Nuridy, Apoteker Suci Gartina, Apoteker Widriyatul Lianah, Apoteker Mahfuzah, serta ahli gizi.
Berdasarkan hasil review tersebut, Marifit direkomendasikan sebagai nutrisi pendamping harian, bukan sebagai obat, untuk membantu menjaga metabolisme tubuh sebagai bagian dari upaya menjaga kesehatan secara menyeluruh, khususnya bagi masyarakat dengan aktivitas padat yang ingin menjaga keseimbangan metabolik terkait gula darah, tekanan darah, dan kolesterol melalui pola hidup sehat.
Menurut Apoteker Suci Gartina, nutrisi pendamping dapat menjadi pelengkap bagi masyarakat modern yang sering kali memiliki pola hidup kurang ideal sehingga kebutuhan nutrisi hariannya tetap dapat terpenuhi.
Baca juga: Kaya Nutrisi dan Serat, Ini 8 Manfaat Edamame Bagi Kesehatan Tubuh
Sementara itu, Apoteker Widriyatul Lianah menilai kombinasi ekstrak daun kelor dan daun bidara memberikan nilai tambah karena menghadirkan berbagai kandungan nutrisi dan antioksidan alami yang mendukung kebutuhan tubuh sehari-hari, termasuk dalam membantu menjaga keseimbangan metabolisme.
Pendapat serupa disampaikan Apoteker Mahfuzah. Ia mengatakan Marifit dapat menjadi bagian dari rutinitas sehat harian untuk melengkapi pola makan bergizi seimbang, namun bukan untuk menggantikan makanan utama maupun terapi medis dari tenaga kesehatan.
Ekstrak daun kelor dalam Marifit diketahui mengandung berbagai vitamin, mineral, asam amino, serta antioksidan alami. Sementara itu, daun bidara mengandung berbagai senyawa bioaktif yang turut mendukung kesehatan tubuh.

items.title: John Herdman Bawa 24 Pemain ke Singapura, Timnas Indonesia Incar Tiga Poin Harga Mati
items.summary: John Herdman bawa 24 pemain dalam laga hidup mati melawan Singapura. Skuad Garuda wajib menang demi tiket lolos ke semifinal Piala AFF 2026.
items.body_text:
Piala AFF 2026
John Herdman Bawa 24 Pemain ke Singapura, Timnas Indonesia Incar Tiga Poin Harga Mati
John Herdman bawa 24 pemain dalam laga hidup mati melawan Singapura. Skuad Garuda wajib menang demi tiket lolos ke semifinal Piala AFF 2026.
Ringkasan Berita:
- Timnas Indonesia menghadapi laga hidup mati melawan Singapura pada Jumat (7/8/2026). Skuad Garuda wajib menang demi dapat lolos ke semifinal Piala AFF 2026.
- Ketua BTN Sumardji menilai evaluasi utama usai kalah 0-3 dari Vietnam adalah aspek mental pemain. Ia meminta Garuda tampil lebih siap, disiplin, dan pantang meremehkan lawan.
- John Herdman membawa 24 pemain ke Singapura. Justin Hubner absen karena ditahan Fortuna Sittard, sementara Marselino Ferdinan dipastikan menepi akibat cedera.
TRIBUNNEWS.COM - Timnas Indonesia bakal menghadapi laga penentuan Grup A Piala AFF 2026 melawan Singapura yang akan digelar di Stadion Jalan Besar, Jumat (7/8/2026).
Pertandingan tersebut menjadi duel hidup mati bagi Skuad Garuda. Tim besutan John Herdman diwajibkan meraih kemenangan demi menjaga asa lolos ke babak semifinal.
Saat ini, Timnas Indonesia berada di peringkat ketiga klasemen sementara Grup A. Karena itu, tambahan tiga poin menjadi target mutlak jika ingin melanjutkan perjalanan di turnamen sepak bola Asia Tenggara tersebut.
Timnas Indonesia sendiri telah bertolak ke Singapura pada Rabu (5/8/2026) kemarin.
Keberangkatan kali ini dilakukan lebih awal dibandingkan laga tandang sebelumnya ke markas Timor Leste.
Jika sebelumnya tim baru bertolak sehari sebelum pertandingan, kali ini Rizky Ridho dan kolega sudah terbang dua hari sebelum kick-off.
Langkah tersebut diharapkan memberi waktu lebih bagi para pemain untuk memulihkan kondisi sekaligus mematangkan persiapan jelang pertandingan krusial.
Timnas Indonesia juga berupaya bangkit setelah menelan kekalahan 0-3 dari Vietnam pada laga sebelumnya yang berlangsung di Stadion Pakansari, Bogor.
Hasil tersebut menjadi bahan evaluasi tim pelatih, terutama dari sisi kesiapan mental pemain.
Ketua Badan Tim Nasional (BTN), Sumardji, mengungkapkan bahwa aspek psikologis menjadi perhatian utama setelah kekalahan dari Vietnam.
Menurutnya, para pemain belum mampu memberikan respons yang tepat ketika pertandingan berjalan tidak sesuai harapan.
"Evaluasi dilakukan kemarin yang nomor satu adalah bagaimana mental pemain," ujar Sumardji dalam program Sapa Indonesia Malam di Kompas TV, Selasa (4/8/2026).
"Yang menjadikan anak-anak tak bisa merespons dengan cepat Vietnam adalah persiapan mental diri itu kurang."
"Satu sisi menganggap lawan yang dihadapi itu biasa-biasa saja."
"Respons itu tidak segera ditangkap oleh pemain," lanjutnya.

PSEi dips as investors await GDP data
MANILA, Philippines — Local stocks ended slightly lower on Thursday as investors stayed on the sidelines ahead of the release of the Philippines’ economic growth data, while geopolitical tensions in the Middle East continued to dampen risk appetite.
The benchmark Philippine Stock Exchange Index (PSEi) slipped 0.13 percent, or 8.36 points, to close at 6,277.95.
READ: Inflation eased further to 6.2% in July
According to Philstocks Financial Inc., investors remained cautious as they awaited the country’s gross domestic product figures, which could provide fresh clues on the strength of the local economy.
Geopolitical jitters dampen risk appetite
Uncertainty between the US and Iran also weighed on sentiment after Tehran denied reports of ongoing talks.
READ: Iran says close to Hormuz plan with Oman, but reopening depends on US
Luis Limlingan, head of sales at Regina Capital Development Corp., said a rise in unemployment in the latest labor report further dampened sentiment and raised concerns over domestic economic momentum.
“As a result, risk appetite stayed subdued, with investors opting to trim positions while awaiting clearer signals on the country’s growth outlook,” Limlingan said.
Despite the weak finish, bargain hunting in the final minutes of trading helped trim earlier losses.
Trading activity remained subdued, with net value turnover reaching P5.64 billion, reflecting the cautious mood among investors.
Foreign investors also stayed on the selling side, posting net outflows of P323.68 million.
Sectors posted mixed performance. The industrial index led the gainers after climbing 0.97 percent, while the services sector posted the steepest decline, falling 0.44 percent.
Among individual stocks, DigiPlus Interactive Corp. emerged as the session’s top performer on the benchmark index, rising 3.26 percent to P9.50.
Meanwhile, Bank of the Philippine Islands was the biggest laggard, dropping 2.32 percent to P101 per share.
Analysts said investors are likely to remain cautious in the near term as they assess incoming economic data and monitor global developments, particularly geopolitical risks that could continue to influence market sentiment. /pai

City scholarship overhaul: Budget constraints driving stricter eligibility
CEBU CITY, Philippines — A proposed ordinance that seeks to revise Cebu City’s scholarship program drew scrutiny from council members after its proponents acknowledged that the measure primarily aims to limit the number of qualified applicants because of mounting budget constraints.
Several provisions also sparked concerns of confusing eligibility rules.
During a public hearing on August 4, members of the Cebu City Council questioned whether the amendments to the Cebu City Scholarship Program would actually achieve their stated objective or instead create new ambiguities that could unfairly disqualify students.
Councilor Winston Pepito, the ordinance’s principal proponent, openly said the proposed amendments intend to narrow eligibility rather than expand it.
“We have a problem with the budget. That’s why this amendatory ordinance is not to embrace more. This is limiting,” Pepito said.
READ: Cebu expands medical scholarship to 72 students, eyes more doctors for provincial hospitals
He cited instances where students allegedly transferred to Cebu City only during their final years of high school and later qualified for the city’s scholarship program despite completing most of their education elsewhere.
“That was the intention why we introduced these amendments,” he said.
Budget, residency concerns
Scholarship Office Executive Director Shirley Otadoy supported the proposed revisions, saying existing rules allowed applicants who had only recently transferred to Cebu City to qualify for scholarships.
She said the office previously relied mainly on applicants’ senior high school diplomas, making it possible for students who enrolled in Cebu City only during the latter part of high school to become eligible.
To address this, the proposed ordinance requires most applicants from private schools to demonstrate a longer educational history within Cebu City’s public school system.
Under the draft measure:
- Public high school graduates must have completed both junior high school (Grades 7 to 10) and senior high school (Grades 11 and 12) in a public school within Cebu City.
- Private senior high school graduates who studied under government vouchers or institutional scholarships must have completed junior high school in a Cebu City public school.
- Applicants who also attended private junior high school must prove they completed elementary education in a Cebu City public elementary school before becoming eligible.
The ordinance also opens eligibility to private school students who completed elementary through senior high school in Cebu City under academic scholarships or government grants, provided they submit proof of their scholarship and show that their parents or guardians earn no more than ₱250,000 annually.
Council questions restrictive requirements
Several councilors, however, argued that some provisions either contradict the ordinance’s stated purpose or impose unnecessary requirements.
Councilor Philip Zafra questioned the wording of the proposed qualifications, particularly the phrase stating that public high school graduates qualify “regardless of where elementary education was completed.”
He argued that the language appears inconsistent with other provisions requiring certain private school applicants to prove they completed elementary education in a public school.
Zafra also challenged the scholarship office’s reliance on its implementing rules and regulations (IRR).
“The IRR should not go beyond what is provided in the ordinance. The IRR is not the law,” Zafra said.
He stressed that implementing rules cannot impose requirements not expressly authorized by the ordinance itself.
Later in the hearing, Zafra urged the proponents to simplify the qualifications by focusing primarily on senior high school graduates since the scholarship program targets college students.
He also questioned why the draft introduces the term “legal guardian” without defining it

items.title: What we know about North Korean forces joining Russia’s war against Ukraine
items.summary: North Korea has supplied Russia with millions of artillery and mortar rounds, ballistic missiles, long-range artillery and multiple-launch rocket systems, according to Ukrainian and independent assessments
items.body_text:
AT A GLANCE
SEOUL, South Korea – North Korea has deployed troops, weapons and now, according to a Ukrainian intelligence official, a missile unit to support Russia’s war against Ukraine, marking Pyongyang’s most significant involvement in a war since the 1950s.
Here is what is known about the growing military ties:
What are the latest reports?
A North Korean missile unit has begun deploying to western Russia and could be equipped with up to 120 ballistic missiles and six launchers for attacks on Ukraine, an official at Ukraine’s GUR military intelligence agency said.
The unit comprises about 90 North Korean personnel and is expected to be based in Russia’s Voronezh region, the official said.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in July that Russia wanted to bring in another 30,000 North Korean troops and was preparing facilities in Voronezh to receive them.
Reuters could not independently verify the claims.
How many North Korean troops have been sent?
Ukrainian, US, and South Korean assessments initially put the deployment at 10,000 to 12,000 troops in late 2024.
In January 2025, the US deputy ambassador to the United Nations said more than 12,000 North Korean soldiers were in Russia.
Later Ukrainian and South Korean estimates put the number of troops in Russia’s Kursk region at about 14,000 to 15,000.
The Ukrainian official said this month that around 9,500 North Korean troops remained in Kursk, but were not then directly involved in operations against Ukraine.
Russia and North Korea confirmed in April 2025 that North Korean troops had fought Ukrainian forces in Kursk.
Russia’s top military commander praised their role after Moscow said it had retaken Kursk territory, while Pyongyang said the deployment was ordered by leader Kim Jong-un.
What other personnel has North Korea said it will provide?
In June 2025, Russian Security Council Secretary Sergei Shoigu said North Korea would send 1,000 sappers and 5,000 military construction workers to Kursk to clear mines and help rebuild infrastructure damaged in the fighting.
That same month, South Korean lawmakers, citing a briefing by the National Intelligence Service, said that North Korea appeared to have begun recruiting personnel for an additional deployment to Russia, while continuing to supply Russia with artillery ammunition and missiles in exchange for economic cooperation and technical assistance.
It remains unclear how many engineers, deminers or additional troops have arrived in Russia, or whether they have been used in combat roles.
What weapons has North Korea provided?
North Korea has supplied Russia with millions of artillery and mortar rounds, ballistic missiles, long-range artillery and multiple-launch rocket systems, according to Ukrainian and independent assessments.
A Reuters analysis with the UK-based Open Source Centre found four Russian-flagged cargo ships made 64 voyages to North Korea’s Rajin port between September 2023 and March 2025, transporting nearly 16,000 containers of ammunition to Russian ports.
Ukrainian officials said North Korea was supplying about half of the munitions Russia needed on the front lines.
Ukraine’s GUR military intelligence agency said that North Korea had delivered 4 million artillery shells from mid-2023, excluding mortar rounds. It said North Korea had supplied 148 KN-23 and KN-24 ballistic missiles by the start of 2025.
Why is North Korea helping Russia?
Russian President Vladimir Putin and North Korean leader Kim signed a comprehensive strategic partnership treaty during Putin’s June 2024 visit to Pyongyang. The pact includes a mutual assistance provision if either country faces external aggression.
North Korea has cast its deployment as assistance to a treaty partner. Kim said in May 2025 that participation in the war was justified as an exercise of North Korea’s sovereign rights in defence of a “brother nation.”
Analysts say Pyongyang stands to gain hard currency, oil and other economic support, as well as access to

items.title: Court of Appeals asked to void SEC rule imposing term limits for broker directors
items.summary: Long-time PSE broker directors Eddie Gobing and Vivian Yuchengco want the SEC to stop implementing a May 21 circular on term limits
items.body_text:
AT A GLANCE
MANILA, Philippines – Long-time Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) broker directors filed a petition with the Court of Appeals, challenging the Securities and Exchange Commission’s (SEC) rule that set term limits for broker directors.
SEC Memorandum Circular No. 17-2026 prescribes a cumulative 10-year term limit for broker directors, whether consecutive or intermittent. The memorandum prescribes a penalty of P1 million per broker per year, and a continuing penalty of P30,000 for every month that a broker director holds a seat in violation of the circular.
“[Declare] SEC MC No. 17, series of 2026 unconstitutional for violating Petitioners’ rights to due process and equal protection and VOID for being contrary to the Securities Regulation Code and Revised Corporation Code,” read part of the 56-page petition filed by Eddie Gobing and Vivian Yuchengco.
Gobing and Yuchengco also want the CA to order the SEC to stop implementing the circular dated May 21, 2026.
The broker directors filed a petition for certiorari and prohibition, which is used to seek a review of another body’s decision or ruling.
“Petitioners submit that the imposition of maximum term limits for Broker Directors of the PSE – the only Exchange in the Philippines – was attended with grave abuse of discretion amounting to lack or excess of jurisdiction on the part of the SEC,” the petition read. “The Assailed Circular violates the due process and equal protection clause of the Constitution and is ultra vires or beyond the limits of the authority conferred on the SEC by its enabling statutes.”
PSE is a self-regulatory body that ensures “a fair, efficient, transparent and orderly market for the buying, and selling of securities.”
Gobing has a cumulative term of 27 years with the PSE, while Yuchengco has 29 years.
Before the SEC memorandum, broker directors of exchanges may hold their positions as long as they are duly elected by the stockholders.
Under the new SEC rules, broker directors may be elected for a term of only a year, with a maximum of 10 cumulative years. But the one decade period cannot be served continuously.
After serving five years, either consecutive or intermittent, a broker director shall have a one-year cooling-off period before they can be reelected again.
The SEC memorandum cites a principle of the International Organization of Securities Commissions which states that “the length of board members’ terms of office would be relevant in assessing shareholders’ ability to participate actively in the nomination and election of board members.” – Rappler.com

items.summary: EJ Obiena claims his seventh first-place finish of the year and second straight in Germany as he rules 30th International Pole Vault Meeting in Jockgrim
items.body_text:
MANILA, Philippines – EJ Obiena’s bid to return to world top 10 continues to gain ground.
Obiena captured back-to-back gold medals after ruling the 30th International Pole Vault Meeting in Jockgrim, Germany, on Wednesday, August 5 (Thursday, August 6, Manila time).
The Filipino cleared 5.83 meters and beat Qatar’s Seifeldin Abdelsalam via countback to claim his seventh first-place finish of the year.
It marked Obiena’s second consecutive gold medal in Germany following his victory in the 1st International Pole Vault Meeting in Halberstad, where he tallied 5.76m.
The former world No. 2, Obiena previously said that a “realistic goal” for him is to once again crack the top 10, and he is slowly working towards that target as he climbed to No. 13 from No. 14 last week in the world rankings.
Obiena has shown consistency, clearing the 5.80m bar for the fourth time in his last five meets.
“Was far from smooth competition and some struggles during warmup and earlier bars but happy to scrape an 80 bar. We continue to work and now a few trainings in before we go again,” Obiena wrote on his social media accounts.
Obiena took two tries to hurdle 5.45m but needed just a single attempt in each of the next three heights as he vaulted past 5.60m, 6.70m, and 5.83m.
Eyeing his first 5.90m-clearance since his fourth-place outing in the 2024 Paris Olympics, the 30-year-old Filipino star gave 5.93m a go but to no avail.
Abdelsalam settled for silver after three ties at 5.83m, while Turkey’s Ersu Sasma bagged bronze with 5.77m.
Now based in Athens, Greece, Obiena goes back to work with the team of current world No. 2 Emmanouil Karalis. – Rappler.com

items.title: US formally transmits Quiboloy extradition request – Philippine Embassy
items.summary: The formal request was transmitted to the Philippine DOJ, Philippine Ambassador Romualdez says.
items.body_text:
US formally transmits Quiboloy extradition request – Philippine Embassy
MANILA, Philippines — Nearly a year after Washington's bid to extradite Apollo Quiboloy first became public, the United States has formally transmitted its request to the Philippine government, Philippine Ambassador to the US Jose Manuel Romualdez confirmed Thursday.
"The formal request was transmitted to the Department of Justice," Romualdez told Philstar.com in a message.
The development advances an extradition effort first disclosed in August 2025, when Romualdez said Washington had asked the Philippines to turn over the Kingdom of Jesus Christ founder and sent supporting documents to the DOJ.
The Department of Justice, however, said Thursday that it had not officially received any document indicating that the United States had formally requested Quiboloy's extradition.
"Under the Philippine-US Extradition Treaty and applicable law, the DFA would be the first point of contact for such a request. Initial inquiries may therefore be directed to the DFA," the DOJ said.
The development marks the formal step needed for Philippine authorities to begin evaluating Washington's request under the countries' extradition treaty.
US charges. Quiboloy was indicted by a US federal grand jury in 2021 on charges that include conspiracy to engage in sex trafficking by force, fraud and coercion and sex trafficking of children.
He also faces substantive sex trafficking, conspiracy and bulk cash smuggling charges, according to the Federal Bureau of Investigation.
US prosecutors accused Quiboloy and other Kingdom of Jesus Christ officials of recruiting women and girls to serve as his personal assistants and coercing them into sex.
Quiboloy has denied the allegations.
Philippine cases
Quiboloy remains detained while facing child and sexual abuse charges before a Quezon City court.
He and several co-accused are also facing non-bailable qualified human trafficking charges before a Pasig court.
The pending Philippine cases may affect the timing of any extradition. The DOJ said in 2025 that local jurisdiction generally takes priority, although the courts ultimately act on extradition proceedings.
Under Philippine law, the DOJ evaluates a formal extradition request and, if it finds the documents sufficient, assigns a government lawyer to file a petition before a trial court.
Quiboloy was taken into custody on Sept. 8, 2024, following a prolonged police operation at the Kingdom of Jesus Christ compound in Davao City.

Walang Pasok: Class suspensions for August 7 due to habagat, 'Maymay'
MANILA, Philippines — Several local government units have announced class suspensions for Friday, August 7, due to the continuing effects of the southwest monsoon or habagat and Tropical Depression Maymay (international name: Kujira).
Maymay made landfall in Magsingal, Ilocos Sur before dawn Thursday and moved over Bangued, Abra later in the morning as it crossed Northern Luzon. By Thursday afternoon, however, PAGASA said the cyclone had weakened into a tropical depression while moving east-southeast over the Cordillera region.
Signal No. 1 remains hoisted over parts of Northern Luzon, while the weather bureau warned that the combined effects of Maymay and the southwest monsoon will continue to bring heavy rains and strong winds.
Meanwhile, PAGASA is also monitoring Typhoon Dolphin outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR).

items.title: ‘Maymay’ further weakens over Cordilleras
items.summary: As of 2 p.m., the center of Maymay was last estimated in the vicinity of Gamu, Isabela.
items.body_text:
‘Maymay’ further weakens over Cordilleras
MANILA, Philippines — Tropical Depression Maymay (international name: Kujira) has further weakened while moving over the Cordilleras, the state weather bureau PAGASA said.
As of 2 p.m., the center of Maymay was last estimated in the vicinity of Gamu, Isabela.
Maymay now packs maximum sustained winds of 45 kilometers per hour (kph) near the center and gustiness of up to 75 kph, moving east-southeastward at 20 kph.
Despite the cyclone's downgrade, Signal No. 1 remains hoisted over vast portions of Northern and Central Luzon. Areas under Signal No. 1 can expect strong winds ranging from 39 to 61 kph within 36 hours, posing a minimal to minor threat to life and property:
- Ilocos Norte
- Ilocos Sur
- La Union
- Northwestern portion of Pangasinan (Bolinao, Anda, Bani)
- Apayao
- Abra
- Kalinga
- Mountain Province
- Ifugao
- Benguet
- Mainland Cagayan
- Isabela
- Quirino
- Nueva Vizcaya
- Northern and central portions of Aurora (Dilasag, Casiguran, Dinalungan, Dipaculao)
PAGASA noted that the combined peripheral effect of Maymay and the enhanced Southwest Monsoon, locally known as habagat, will continue to bring strong to gale-force gusts across most parts of the country through Saturday, August 8.
The state weather bureau forecasts Maymay to traverse the mountainous terrain of Northern Luzon before emerging over the eastern coastal waters of Isabela within the next 12 hours.
PAGASA expects Maymay to downgrade into a remnant low by Thursday afternoon or evening, which will then move southeastward until it eventually merges into the circulation of Tropical Cyclone Dolphin.

items.title: UK gets first 'super-university' as Kent and Greenwich merge into higher education giant
items.summary: With dozens of U.K. universities under financial pressure and some at risk of insolvency, the Universities of Kent and Greenwich have merged to create Britain's first "super-university," a move they say will bolster their long-term financial resilience.
items.body_text:
The newly formed London and South East University Group (LASE), set to launch in September, spans four campuses across London, Medway, and Kent.
It will become the nation's third-largest higher education institution, with approximately 50,000 students, sitting behind the Open University (around 125,000 students) and University College London (just over 50,000 students).
The new multi-university group, billed as the U.K.'s first "super-university," introduces a first-of-its-kind model that brings the two institutions under a single umbrella while allowing each to retain its own name, identity, academic programs, and local presence.
"It is designed to enable other universities to join in the future," the University of Kent said on its website.
Despite the merger, the University of Kent and the University of Greenwich will continue to operate under their existing names as separate academic divisions within LASE.
Students will continue to apply to, study at, and graduate from their chosen university, The Independent reported.
Kent and Greenwich leaders noted that combining operations will strengthen their financial standing and could serve as a model for other universities navigating similar economic challenges.
"The combined entity will provide a strong financial foundation to weather current and future economic challenges, widen access to higher education, address skills gaps and inequalities, and increase research capacity, particularly in shared priority areas, such as food security and sustainability, health and wellbeing and the creative industries," the University of Kent stated on its website.
"Its collective power will enable it to tackle real world issues with greater impact locally, nationally and globally," the statement continued.
Professor Jane Harrington, Vice-Chancellor of the University of Greenwich and the new Chief Executive of LASE, said the new model enables the two schools to build on their 20-year cooperation.
"This is a truly significant moment for the sector, which we hope could provide a blueprint for other institutions in the future. We are bringing our institutions together within a unique new group structure whilst being able to retain the strength of our individual trading names and longstanding university identities."
The move comes as Britain's higher education sector faces mounting financial strain.
According to the Office for Students (OfS), England's higher education regulator, 24 institutions were at risk of becoming insolvent within a year of last November. Nearly half of all higher education providers are projected to run deficits during the 2025-26 academic year.
A report released in May by MPs on the education select committee warned that the higher education sector was "facing a financial crisis" and that there was "a clear possibility of a university closing," according The Guardian.
It noted that the report highlighted many universities had already cut jobs, sold buildings or land, and discontinued courses.
As for LASE's operation, the U.K. Visas and Immigration has confirmed that all existing student visa sponsorship arrangements with the Universities of Greenwich and Kent will seamlessly transfer to the new multi-university group, according to the University of Kent's website.
The university added that there will be no changes to existing student loan arrangements as a result of the merger.
A new Chancellor, governing body, and senior executive team for LASE have been appointed and officially took up their roles earlier this week, the University of Greenwich announced.
